nodes.label: 3DModel
nodes.description:
A 3D model represents some kind of 3D content, which may have [[encoding]]s in one or more [[MediaObject]]s. Many 3D formats are available (e.g. see [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Category:3D_graphics_file_formats)); specific encoding formats can be represented using the [[encodingFormat]] property applied to the relevant [[MediaObject]]. For the
case of a single file published after Zip compression, the convention of appending '+zip' to the [[encodingFormat]] can be used. Geospatial, AR/VR, artistic/animation, gaming, engineering and scientific content can all be represented using [[3DModel]].

nodes.label: AMRadioChannel
nodes.description: A radio channel that uses AM.

nodes.label: APIReference
nodes.description: Reference documentation for application programming interfaces (APIs).

nodes.label: Abdomen
nodes.description: Abdomen clinical examination.

nodes.label: AboutPage
nodes.description: Web page type: About page.

nodes.label: AcceptAction
nodes.description:
The act of committing to/adopting an object.

Related actions:

* [[RejectAction]]: The antonym of AcceptAction.

nodes.label: Accommodation
nodes.description:
An accommodation is a place that can accommodate human beings, e.g. a hotel room, a camping pitch, or a meeting room. Many accommodations are for overnight stays, but this is not a mandatory requirement. For more specific types of accommodations not defined in schema.org, one can use [[additionalType]] with external vocabularies.

See also the dedicated document on the use of schema.org for marking up hotels and other forms of accommodations.

nodes.label: AccountingService
nodes.description: Accountancy business.\n\nAs a [[LocalBusiness]] it can be described as a [[provider]] of one or more [[Service]]\(s).

nodes.label: AchieveAction
nodes.description: The act of accomplishing something via previous efforts. It is an instantaneous action rather than an ongoing process.

nodes.label: Action
nodes.description: An action performed by a direct agent and indirect participants upon a direct object. Optionally happens at a location with the help of an inanimate instrument. The execution of the action may produce a result. Specific action sub-type documentation specifies the exact expectation of each argument/role.\n\nSee also [blog post](https://blog.schema.org/2014/04/16/announcing-schema-org-actions/) and [Actions overview document](https://schema.org/docs/actions.html).

nodes.label: ActionAccessSpecification
nodes.description: A set of requirements that must be fulfilled in order to perform an Action.

nodes.label: ActionStatusType
nodes.description: The status of an Action.

nodes.label: ActivateAction
nodes.description: The act of starting or activating a device or application (e.g. starting a timer or turning on a flashlight).

nodes.label: ActivationFee
nodes.description: Represents the activation fee part of the total price for an offered product, for example a cellphone contract.

nodes.label: ActiveActionStatus
nodes.description: An in-progress action (e.g., while watching the movie, or driving to a location).

nodes.label: ActiveNotRecruiting
nodes.description: Active, but not recruiting new participants.

nodes.label: AddAction
nodes.description: The act of editing by adding an object to a collection.

nodes.label: AdministrativeArea
nodes.description: A geographical region, typically under the jurisdiction of a particular government.

nodes.label: AdultEntertainment
nodes.description: An adult entertainment establishment.

nodes.label: AdultOrientedEnumeration
nodes.description: Enumeration of considerations that make a product relevant or potentially restricted for adults only.

nodes.label: AdvertiserContentArticle
nodes.description: An [[Article]] that an external entity has paid to place or to produce to its specifications. Includes [advertorials](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Advertorial), sponsored content, native advertising and other paid content.

nodes.label: AerobicActivity
nodes.description: Physical activity of relatively low intensity that depends primarily on the aerobic energy-generating process; during activity, the aerobic metabolism uses oxygen to adequately meet energy demands during exercise.

nodes.label: AggregateOffer
nodes.description: When a single product is associated with multiple offers (for example, the same pair of shoes is offered by different merchants), then AggregateOffer can be used.\n\nNote: AggregateOffers are normally expected to associate multiple offers that all share the same defined [[businessFunction]] value, or default to http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Sell if businessFunction is not explicitly defined.

nodes.label: AggregateRating
nodes.description: The average rating based on multiple ratings or reviews.

nodes.label: AgreeAction
nodes.description: The act of expressing a consistency of opinion with the object. An agent agrees to/about an object (a proposition, topic or theme) with participants.

nodes.label: Airline
nodes.description: An organization that provides flights for passengers.

nodes.label: Airport
nodes.description: An airport.

nodes.label: AlbumRelease
nodes.description: AlbumRelease.

nodes.label: AlcoholConsideration
nodes.description: Item contains alcohol or promotes alcohol consumption.

nodes.label: AlgorithmicMediaDigitalSource
nodes.description: Content coded as 'algorithmic media' using the IPTC digital source type vocabulary.

nodes.label: AlgorithmicallyEnhancedDigitalSource
nodes.description: Content coded as 'algorithmically enhanced' using the IPTC digital source type vocabulary.

nodes.label: AlignmentObject
nodes.description:
An intangible item that describes an alignment between a learning resource and a node in an educational framework.
Should not be used where the nature of the alignment can be described using a simple property, for example to express that a resource [[teaches]] or [[assesses]] a competency.

nodes.label: AllWheelDriveConfiguration
nodes.description: All-wheel Drive is a transmission layout where the engine drives all four wheels.

nodes.label: AllergiesHealthAspect
nodes.description: Content about the allergy-related aspects of a health topic.

nodes.label: AllocateAction
nodes.description: The act of organizing tasks/objects/events by associating resources to it.

nodes.label: AmpStory
nodes.description: A creative work with a visual storytelling format intended to be viewed online, particularly on mobile devices.

nodes.label: AmusementPark
nodes.description: An amusement park.

nodes.label: AnaerobicActivity
nodes.description: Physical activity that is of high-intensity which utilizes the anaerobic metabolism of the body.

nodes.label: AnalysisNewsArticle
nodes.description: An AnalysisNewsArticle is a [[NewsArticle]] that, while based on factual reporting, incorporates the expertise of the author/producer, offering interpretations and conclusions.

nodes.label: AnatomicalStructure
nodes.description: Any part of the human body, typically a component of an anatomical system. Organs, tissues, and cells are all anatomical structures.

nodes.label: AnatomicalSystem
nodes.description: An anatomical system is a group of anatomical structures that work together to perform a certain task. Anatomical systems, such as organ systems, are one organizing principle of anatomy, and can include circulatory, digestive, endocrine, integumentary, immune, lymphatic, muscular, nervous, reproductive, respiratory, skeletal, urinary, vestibular, and other systems.

nodes.label: AndroidPlatform
nodes.description: Represents the broad notion of Android-based operating systems.

nodes.label: Anesthesia
nodes.description: A specific branch of medical science that pertains to study of anesthetics and their application.

nodes.label: AnimalShelter
nodes.description: Animal shelter.

nodes.label: Answer
nodes.description: An answer offered to a question; perhaps correct, perhaps opinionated or wrong.

nodes.label: Apartment
nodes.description: An apartment (in American English) or flat (in British English) is a self-contained housing unit (a type of residential real estate) that occupies only part of a building (source: Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia, see http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apartment).

nodes.label: ApartmentComplex
nodes.description: Residence type: Apartment complex.

nodes.label: Appearance
nodes.description: Appearance assessment with clinical examination.

nodes.label: AppendAction
nodes.description: The act of inserting at the end if an ordered collection.

nodes.label: ApplyAction
nodes.description:
The act of registering to an organization/service without the guarantee to receive it.

Related actions:

* [[RegisterAction]]: Unlike RegisterAction, ApplyAction has no guarantees that the application will be accepted.

nodes.label: ApprovedIndication
nodes.description: An indication for a medical therapy that has been formally specified or approved by a regulatory body that regulates use of the therapy; for example, the US FDA approves indications for most drugs in the US.

nodes.label: Aquarium
nodes.description: Aquarium.

nodes.label: ArchiveComponent
nodes.description: An intangible type to be applied to any archive content, carrying with it a set of properties required to describe archival items and collections.

nodes.label: ArchiveOrganization
nodes.description: An organization with archival holdings. An organization which keeps and preserves archival material and typically makes it accessible to the public.

nodes.label: ArriveAction
nodes.description: The act of arriving at a place. An agent arrives at a destination from a fromLocation, optionally with participants.

nodes.label: ArtGallery
nodes.description: An art gallery.

nodes.label: Artery
nodes.description: A type of blood vessel that specifically carries blood away from the heart.

nodes.label: Article
nodes.description: An article, such as a news article or piece of investigative report. Newspapers and magazines have articles of many different types and this is intended to cover them all.\n\nSee also [blog post](https://blog.schema.org/2014/09/02/schema-org-support-for-bibliographic-relationships-and-periodicals/).

nodes.label: AskAction
nodes.description:
The act of posing a question / favor to someone.

Related actions:

* [[ReplyAction]]: Appears generally as a response to AskAction.

nodes.label: AskPublicNewsArticle
nodes.description: A [[NewsArticle]] expressing an open call by a [[NewsMediaOrganization]] asking the public for input, insights, clarifications, anecdotes, documentation, etc., on an issue, for reporting purposes.

nodes.label: AssessAction
nodes.description: The act of forming one's opinion, reaction or sentiment.

nodes.label: AssignAction
nodes.description: The act of allocating an action/event/task to some destination (someone or something).

nodes.label: Atlas
nodes.description: A collection or bound volume of maps, charts, plates or tables, physical or in media form illustrating any subject.

nodes.label: Attorney
nodes.description: Professional service: Attorney. \n\nThis type is deprecated - [[LegalService]] is more inclusive and less ambiguous.

nodes.label: Audience
nodes.description: Intended audience for an item, i.e. the group for whom the item was created.

nodes.label: AudioObject
nodes.description: An audio file.

nodes.label: AudioObjectSnapshot
nodes.description: A specific and exact (byte-for-byte) version of an [[AudioObject]]. Two byte-for-byte identical files, for the purposes of this type, considered identical. If they have different embedded metadata the files will differ. Different external facts about the files, e.g. creator or dateCreated that aren't represented in their actual content, do not affect this notion of identity.

nodes.label: Audiobook
nodes.description: An audiobook.

nodes.label: AudiobookFormat
nodes.description: Book format: Audiobook. This is an enumerated value for use with the bookFormat property. There is also a type 'Audiobook' in the bib extension which includes Audiobook specific properties.

nodes.label: Audiology
nodes.description: A specific branch of medical science concerned with the diagnosis, management, and non-surgical treatment of hearing, balance, and related auditory processing disorders, including conditions such as tinnitus, hyperacusis, and misophonia.

nodes.label: AuthenticateAction
nodes.description: The action of authenticating into a device or application.

nodes.label: AuthoritativeLegalValue
nodes.description: Indicates that the publisher gives some special status to the publication of the document. ("The Queens Printer" version of a UK Act of Parliament, or the PDF version of a Directive published by the EU Office of Publications). Something "Authoritative" is considered to be also [[OfficialLegalValue]]".

nodes.label: AuthorizeAction
nodes.description: The act of granting permission to an object.

nodes.label: AutoBodyShop
nodes.description: Auto body shop.

nodes.label: AutoDealer
nodes.description: An car dealership.

nodes.label: AutoPartsStore
nodes.description: An auto parts store.

nodes.label: AutoRental
nodes.description: A car rental business.

nodes.label: AutoRepair
nodes.description: Car repair business.

nodes.label: AutoWash
nodes.description: A car wash business.

nodes.label: AutomatedTeller
nodes.description: ATM/cash machine.

nodes.label: AutomotiveBusiness
nodes.description: Car repair, sales, or parts.

nodes.label: Ayurvedic
nodes.description: A system of medicine that originated in India over thousands of years and that focuses on integrating and balancing the body, mind, and spirit.

nodes.label: BackOrder
nodes.description: Indicates that the item is available on back order.

nodes.label: BackgroundNewsArticle
nodes.description: A [[NewsArticle]] providing historical context, definition and detail on a specific topic (aka "explainer" or "backgrounder"). For example, an in-depth article or frequently-asked-questions ([FAQ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FAQ)) document on topics such as Climate Change or the European Union. Other kinds of background material from a non-news setting are often described using [[Book]] or [[Article]], in particular [[ScholarlyArticle]]. See also [[NewsArticle]] for related vocabulary from a learning/education perspective.

nodes.label: Bacteria
nodes.description: Pathogenic bacteria that cause bacterial infection.

nodes.label: Bakery
nodes.description: A bakery.

nodes.label: Balance
nodes.description: Physical activity that is engaged to help maintain posture and balance.

nodes.label: BankAccount
nodes.description: A product or service offered by a bank whereby one may deposit, withdraw or transfer money and in some cases be paid interest.

nodes.label: BankOrCreditUnion
nodes.description: Bank or credit union.

nodes.label: BarOrPub
nodes.description: A bar or pub.

nodes.label: Barcode
nodes.description: An image of a visual machine-readable code such as a barcode or QR code.

nodes.label: BasicIncome
nodes.description: BasicIncome: this is a benefit for basic income.

nodes.label: Beach
nodes.description: Beach.

nodes.label: BeautySalon
nodes.description: Beauty salon.

nodes.label: BedAndBreakfast
nodes.description:
Bed and breakfast.

See also the dedicated document on the use of schema.org for marking up hotels and other forms of accommodations.

nodes.label: BedDetails
nodes.description: An entity holding detailed information about the available bed types, e.g. the quantity of twin beds for a hotel room. For the single case of just one bed of a certain type, you can use bed directly with a text. See also [[BedType]] (under development).

nodes.label: BedType
nodes.description: A type of bed. This is used for indicating the bed or beds available in an accommodation.

nodes.label: BefriendAction
nodes.description:
The act of forming a personal connection with someone (object) mutually/bidirectionally/symmetrically.

Related actions:

* [[FollowAction]]: Unlike FollowAction, BefriendAction implies that the connection is reciprocal.

nodes.label: BenefitsHealthAspect
nodes.description: Content about the benefits and advantages of usage or utilization of topic.

nodes.label: BikeStore
nodes.description: A bike store.

nodes.label: BioChemEntity
nodes.description: Any biological, chemical, or biochemical thing. For example: a protein; a gene; a chemical; a synthetic chemical.

nodes.label: Blog
nodes.description: A [blog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blog), sometimes known as a "weblog". Note that the individual posts ([[BlogPosting]]s) in a [[Blog]] are often colloquially referred to by the same term.

nodes.label: BlogPosting
nodes.description: A blog post.

nodes.label: BloodTest
nodes.description: A medical test performed on a sample of a patient's blood.

nodes.label: BoardingPolicyType
nodes.description: A type of boarding policy used by an airline.

nodes.label: BoatReservation
nodes.description:
A reservation for boat travel.

Note: This type is for information about actual reservations, e.g. in confirmation emails or HTML pages with individual confirmations of reservations. For offers of tickets, use [[Offer]].

nodes.label: BoatTerminal
nodes.description: A terminal for boats, ships, and other water vessels.

nodes.label: BoatTrip
nodes.description: A trip on a commercial ferry line.

nodes.label: BodyMeasurementArm
nodes.description: Arm length (measured between arms/shoulder line intersection and the prominent wrist bone). Used, for example, to fit shirts.

nodes.label: BodyMeasurementBust
nodes.description: Maximum girth of bust. Used, for example, to fit women's suits.

nodes.label: BodyMeasurementChest
nodes.description: Maximum girth of chest. Used, for example, to fit men's suits.

nodes.label: BodyMeasurementFoot
nodes.description: Foot length (measured between end of the most prominent toe and the most prominent part of the heel). Used, for example, to measure socks.

nodes.label: BodyMeasurementHand
nodes.description: Maximum hand girth (measured over the knuckles of the open right hand excluding thumb, fingers together). Used, for example, to fit gloves.

nodes.label: BodyMeasurementHead
nodes.description: Maximum girth of head above the ears. Used, for example, to fit hats.

nodes.label: BodyMeasurementHeight
nodes.description: Body height (measured between crown of head and soles of feet). Used, for example, to fit jackets.

nodes.label: BodyMeasurementHips
nodes.description: Girth of hips (measured around the buttocks). Used, for example, to fit skirts.

nodes.label: BodyMeasurementInsideLeg
nodes.description: Inside leg (measured between crotch and soles of feet). Used, for example, to fit pants.

nodes.label: BodyMeasurementNeck
nodes.description: Girth of neck. Used, for example, to fit shirts.

nodes.label: BodyMeasurementTypeEnumeration
nodes.description: Enumerates types (or dimensions) of a person's body measurements, for example for fitting of clothes.

nodes.label: BodyMeasurementUnderbust
nodes.description: Girth of body just below the bust. Used, for example, to fit women's swimwear.

nodes.label: BodyMeasurementWaist
nodes.description: Girth of natural waistline (between hip bones and lower ribs). Used, for example, to fit pants.

nodes.label: BodyMeasurementWeight
nodes.description: Body weight. Used, for example, to measure pantyhose.

nodes.label: BodyOfWater
nodes.description: A body of water, such as a sea, ocean, or lake.

nodes.label: Bone
nodes.description: Rigid connective tissue that comprises up the skeletal structure of the human body.

nodes.label: Book
nodes.description: A book.

nodes.label: BookFormatType
nodes.description: The publication format of the book.

nodes.label: BookSeries
nodes.description: A series of books. Included books can be indicated with the hasPart property.

nodes.label: BookStore
nodes.description: A bookstore.

nodes.label: BookmarkAction
nodes.description: An agent bookmarks/flags/labels/tags/marks an object.

nodes.label: Boolean
nodes.description: Boolean: True or False.

nodes.label: BorrowAction
nodes.description:
The act of obtaining an object under an agreement to return it at a later date. Reciprocal of LendAction.

Related actions:

* [[LendAction]]: Reciprocal of BorrowAction.

nodes.label: BowlingAlley
nodes.description: A bowling alley.

nodes.label: BrainStructure
nodes.description: Any anatomical structure which pertains to the soft nervous tissue functioning as the coordinating center of sensation and intellectual and nervous activity.

nodes.label: Brand
nodes.description: A brand is a name used by an organization or business person for labeling a product, product group, or similar.

nodes.label: BreadcrumbList
nodes.description: A BreadcrumbList is an ItemList consisting of a chain of linked Web pages, typically described using at least their URL and their name, and typically ending with the current page.\n\nThe [[position]] property is used to reconstruct the order of the items in a BreadcrumbList. The convention is that a breadcrumb list has an [[itemListOrder]] of [[ItemListOrderAscending]] (lower values listed first), and that the first items in this list correspond to the "top" or beginning of the breadcrumb trail, e.g. with a site or section homepage. The specific values of 'position' are not assigned meaning for a BreadcrumbList, but they should be integers, e.g. beginning with '1' for the first item in the list.

nodes.label: Brewery
nodes.description: Brewery.

nodes.label: Bridge
nodes.description: A bridge.

nodes.label: BroadcastChannel
nodes.description: A unique instance of a BroadcastService on a CableOrSatelliteService lineup.

nodes.label: BroadcastEvent
nodes.description: An over the air or online broadcast event.

nodes.label: BroadcastFrequencySpecification
nodes.description: The frequency in MHz and the modulation used for a particular BroadcastService.

nodes.label: BroadcastRelease
nodes.description: BroadcastRelease.

nodes.label: BroadcastService
nodes.description: A delivery service through which content is provided via broadcast over the air or online.

nodes.label: BrokerageAccount
nodes.description: An account that allows an investor to deposit funds and place investment orders with a licensed broker or brokerage firm.

nodes.label: BuddhistTemple
nodes.description: A Buddhist temple.

nodes.label: BusOrCoach
nodes.description: A bus (also omnibus or autobus) is a road vehicle designed to carry passengers. Coaches are luxury buses, usually in service for long distance travel.

nodes.label: BusReservation
nodes.description: A reservation for bus travel. \n\nNote: This type is for information about actual reservations, e.g. in confirmation emails or HTML pages with individual confirmations of reservations. For offers of tickets, use [[Offer]].

nodes.label: BusStation
nodes.description: A bus station.

nodes.label: BusStop
nodes.description: A bus stop.

nodes.label: BusTrip
nodes.description: A trip on a commercial bus line.

nodes.label: BusinessAudience
nodes.description: A set of characteristics belonging to businesses, e.g. who compose an item's target audience.

nodes.label: BusinessEntityType
nodes.description:
A business entity type is a conceptual entity representing the legal form, the size, the main line of business, the position in the value chain, or any combination thereof, of an organization or business person.

Commonly used values:

* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Business
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Enduser
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#PublicInstitution
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Reseller

nodes.label: BusinessEvent
nodes.description: Event type: Business event.

nodes.label: BusinessFunction
nodes.description:
The business function specifies the type of activity or access (i.e., the bundle of rights) offered by the organization or business person through the offer. Typical are sell, rental or lease, maintenance or repair, manufacture / produce, recycle / dispose, engineering / construction, or installation. Proprietary specifications of access rights are also instances of this class.

Commonly used values:

* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#ConstructionInstallation
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Dispose
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#LeaseOut
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Maintain
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#ProvideService
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Repair
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Sell
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Buy

nodes.label: BusinessSupport
nodes.description: BusinessSupport: this is a benefit for supporting businesses.

nodes.label: BuyAction
nodes.description: The act of giving money to a seller in exchange for goods or services rendered. An agent buys an object, product, or service from a seller for a price. Reciprocal of SellAction.

nodes.label: ByBankTransferInAdvance
nodes.description: Payment in advance by bank transfer, equivalent to http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#ByBankTransferInAdvance.

nodes.label: ByInvoice
nodes.description: Payment by invoice, typically after the goods were delivered, equivalent to http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#ByInvoice.

nodes.label: CDCPMDRecord
nodes.description:
A CDCPMDRecord is a data structure representing a record in a CDC tabular data format
      used for hospital data reporting. See [documentation](/docs/cdc-covid.html) for details, and the linked CDC materials for authoritative
      definitions used as the source here.

nodes.label: CDFormat
nodes.description: CDFormat.

nodes.label: COD
nodes.description: Cash on Delivery (COD) payment, equivalent to http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#COD.

nodes.label: CT
nodes.description: X-ray computed tomography imaging.

nodes.label: CableOrSatelliteService
nodes.description: A service which provides access to media programming like TV or radio. Access may be via cable or satellite.

nodes.label: CafeOrCoffeeShop
nodes.description: A cafe or coffee shop.

nodes.label: Campground
nodes.description:
A camping site, campsite, or [[Campground]] is a place used for overnight stay in the outdoors, typically containing individual [[CampingPitch]] locations. 


In British English a campsite is an area, usually divided into a number of pitches, where people can camp overnight using tents or camper vans or caravans; this British English use of the word is synonymous with the American English expression campground. In American English the term campsite generally means an area where an individual, family, group, or military unit can pitch a tent or park a camper; a campground may contain many campsites (source: Wikipedia, see [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Campsite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Campsite)).



See also the dedicated [document on the use of schema.org for marking up hotels and other forms of accommodations](/docs/hotels.html).

nodes.label: CampingPitch
nodes.description:
A [[CampingPitch]] is an individual place for overnight stay in the outdoors, typically being part of a larger camping site, or [[Campground]].


In British English a campsite, or campground, is an area, usually divided into a number of pitches, where people can camp overnight using tents or camper vans or caravans; this British English use of the word is synonymous with the American English expression campground. In American English the term campsite generally means an area where an individual, family, group, or military unit can pitch a tent or park a camper; a campground may contain many campsites.
(Source: Wikipedia, see [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Campsite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Campsite).)


See also the dedicated [document on the use of schema.org for marking up hotels and other forms of accommodations](/docs/hotels.html).

nodes.label: Canal
nodes.description: A canal, like the Panama Canal.

nodes.label: CancelAction
nodes.description:
The act of asserting that a future event/action is no longer going to happen.

Related actions:

* [[ConfirmAction]]: The antonym of CancelAction.

nodes.label: Car
nodes.description: A car is a wheeled, self-powered motor vehicle used for transportation.

nodes.label: CarUsageType
nodes.description: A value indicating a special usage of a car, e.g. commercial rental, driving school, or as a taxi.

nodes.label: Cardiovascular
nodes.description: A specific branch of medical science that pertains to diagnosis and treatment of disorders of heart and vasculature.

nodes.label: CardiovascularExam
nodes.description: Cardiovascular system assessment with clinical examination.

nodes.label: CaseSeries
nodes.description: A case series (also known as a clinical series) is a medical research study that tracks patients with a known exposure given similar treatment or examines their medical records for exposure and outcome. A case series can be retrospective or prospective and usually involves a smaller number of patients than the more powerful case-control studies or randomized controlled trials. Case series may be consecutive or non-consecutive, depending on whether all cases presenting to the reporting authors over a period of time were included, or only a selection.

nodes.label: Cash
nodes.description: Payment using cash, on premises, equivalent to http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Cash.

nodes.label: Casino
nodes.description: A casino.

nodes.label: CassetteFormat
nodes.description: CassetteFormat.

nodes.label: CategoryCode
nodes.description: A Category Code.

nodes.label: CategoryCodeSet
nodes.description: A set of Category Code values.

nodes.label: CatholicChurch
nodes.description: A Catholic church.

nodes.label: CausesHealthAspect
nodes.description: Information about the causes and main actions that gave rise to the topic.

nodes.label: Cemetery
nodes.description: A graveyard.

nodes.label: Certification
nodes.description: A Certification is an official and authoritative statement about a subject, for example a product, service, person, or organization. A certification is typically issued by an indendent certification body, for example a professional organization or government. It formally attests certain characteristics about the subject, for example Organizations can be ISO certified, Food products can be certified Organic or Vegan, a Person can be a certified professional, a Place can be certified for food processing. There are certifications for many domains: regulatory, organizational, recycling, food, efficiency, educational, ecological, etc. A certification is a form of credential, as are accreditations and licenses. Mapped from the [gs1:CertificationDetails](https://www.gs1.org/voc/CertificationDetails) class in the GS1 Web Vocabulary.

nodes.label: CertificationActive
nodes.description: Specifies that a certification is active.

nodes.label: CertificationInactive
nodes.description: Specifies that a certification is inactive (no longer in effect).

nodes.label: CertificationStatusEnumeration
nodes.description: Enumerates the different statuses of a Certification (Active and Inactive).

nodes.label: Chapter
nodes.description: One of the sections into which a book is divided. A chapter usually has a section number or a name.

nodes.label: CharitableIncorporatedOrganization
nodes.description: CharitableIncorporatedOrganization: Non-profit type referring to a Charitable Incorporated Organization (UK).

nodes.label: CheckAction
nodes.description: An agent inspects, determines, investigates, inquires, or examines an object's accuracy, quality, condition, or state.

nodes.label: CheckInAction
nodes.description:
The act of an agent communicating (service provider, social media, etc) their arrival by registering/confirming for a previously reserved service (e.g. flight check-in) or at a place (e.g. hotel), possibly resulting in a result (boarding pass, etc).

Related actions:

* [[CheckOutAction]]: The antonym of CheckInAction.
* [[ArriveAction]]: Unlike ArriveAction, CheckInAction implies that the agent is informing/confirming the start of a previously reserved service.
* [[ConfirmAction]]: Unlike ConfirmAction, CheckInAction implies that the agent is informing/confirming the *start* of a previously reserved service rather than its validity/existence.

nodes.label: CheckInAdvance
nodes.description: Payment in advance by sending a check, equivalent to http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#CheckInAdvance.

nodes.label: CheckOutAction
nodes.description:

Related actions:

* [[DepartAction]]: Unlike DepartAction, CheckOutAction implies that the agent is informing/confirming the end of a previously reserved service.
* [[CancelAction]]: Unlike CancelAction, CheckOutAction implies that the agent is informing/confirming the end of a previously reserved service.

nodes.label: Claim
nodes.description:
A [[Claim]] in Schema.org represents a specific, factually-oriented claim that could be the [[itemReviewed]] in a [[ClaimReview]]. The content of a claim can be summarized with the [[text]] property. Variations on well known claims can have their common identity indicated via [[sameAs]] links, and summarized with a [[name]]. Ideally, a [[Claim]] description includes enough contextual information to minimize the risk of ambiguity or inclarity. In practice, many claims are better understood in the context in which they appear or the interpretations provided by claim reviews.

  Beyond [[ClaimReview]], the Claim type can be associated with related creative works - for example a [[ScholarlyArticle]] or [[Question]] might be [[about]] some [[Claim]].

  At this time, Schema.org does not define any types of relationship between claims. This is a natural area for future exploration.

nodes.label: ClaimReview
nodes.description: A fact-checking review of claims made (or reported) in some creative work (referenced via itemReviewed).

nodes.label: Clip

nodes.label: CohortStudy
nodes.description: Also known as a panel study. A cohort study is a form of longitudinal study used in medicine and social science. It is one type of study design and should be compared with a cross-sectional study.  A cohort is a group of people who share a common characteristic or experience within a defined period (e.g., are born, leave school, lose their job, are exposed to a drug or a vaccine, etc.). The comparison group may be the general population from which the cohort is drawn, or it may be another cohort of persons thought to have had little or no exposure to the substance under investigation, but otherwise similar. Alternatively, subgroups within the cohort may be compared with each other.

nodes.label: Collection
nodes.description: A collection of items, e.g. creative works or products.

nodes.label: CollegeOrUniversity

nodes.label: ComicCoverArt

nodes.label: ComicIssue
nodes.description:
Individual comic issues are serially published as
    	part of a larger series. For the sake of consistency, even one-shot issues
    	belong to a series comprised of a single issue. All comic issues can be

A sequential publication of comic stories under a

nodes.label: ComicStory
nodes.description:
The term "story" is any indivisible, re-printable
    	unit of a comic, including the interior stories, covers, and backmatter. Most

nodes.label: Comment
nodes.description: A comment on an item - for example, a comment on a blog post. The comment's content is expressed via the [[text]] property, and its topic via [[about]], properties shared with all CreativeWorks.

nodes.label: CommentAction

nodes.label: CommentPermission

nodes.label: CommunicateAction

nodes.label: CommunityHealth

nodes.label: CompilationAlbum

nodes.label: CompleteDataFeed
nodes.description:
A [[CompleteDataFeed]] is a [[DataFeed]] whose standard representation includes content for every item currently in the feed.

This is the equivalent of Atom's element as defined in Feed Paging and Archiving [RFC 5005](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5005), for example (and as defined for Atom), when using data from a feed that represents a collection of items that varies over time (e.g. "Top Twenty Records") there is no need to have newer entries mixed in alongside older, obsolete entries. By marking this feed as a CompleteDataFeed, old entries can be safely discarded when the feed is refreshed, since we can assume the feed has provided descriptions for all current items.

nodes.description: Completed.

nodes.description: A compound price specification is one that bundles multiple prices that all apply in combination for different dimensions of consumption. The ConstraintNode type is provided to support usecases in which a node in a structured data graph is described with properties which appear to describe a single entity, but are being used in a situation where they serve a more abstract purpose. A [[ConstraintNode]] can be described using [[constraintProperty]] and [[numConstraints]]. These constraint properties can serve a
    variety of purposes, and their values may sometimes be understood to indicate sets of possible values rather than single, exact and specific values.

nodes.label: CreativeWorkSeries
nodes.description:
A CreativeWorkSeries in schema.org is a group of related items, typically but not necessarily of the same kind. CreativeWorkSeries are usually organized into some order, often chronological. Unlike [[ItemList]] which is a general purpose data structure for lists of things, the emphasis with CreativeWorkSeries is on published materials (written e.g. books and periodicals, or media such as TV, radio and games).

Specific subtypes are available for describing [[TVSeries]], [[RadioSeries]], [[MovieSeries]], [[BookSeries]], [[Periodical]] and [[VideoGameSeries]]. In each case, the [[hasPart]] / [[isPartOf]] properties can be used to relate the CreativeWorkSeries to its parts. The general CreativeWorkSeries type serves largely just to organize these more specific and practical subtypes.

It is common for properties applicable to an item from the series to be usefully applied to the containing group. Schema.org attempts to anticipate some of these cases, but publishers should be free to apply properties of the series parts to the series as a whole wherever they seem appropriate.

These can include online columns, travel and food guides, TV and radio shows, blogs and other independent Web sites. [[CriticReview]]s are typically more in-depth and professionally written. For simpler, casually written user/visitor/viewer/customer reviews, it is more appropriate to use the [[UserReview]] type. Review aggregator sites such as Metacritic already separate out the site's user reviews from selected critic reviews that originate from third-party sources.

nodes.description: A DatedMoneySpecification represents monetary values with optional start and end dates. For example, this could represent an employee's salary over a specific period of time. __Note:__ This type has been superseded by [[MonetaryAmount]], use of that type is recommended.

nodes.label: DayOfWeek
nodes.description:
The day of the week, e.g. used to specify to which day the opening hours of an OpeningHoursSpecification refer.

Originally, URLs from [GoodRelations](http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1) were used (for [[Monday]], [[Tuesday]], [[Wednesday]], [[Thursday]], [[Friday]], [[Saturday]], [[Sunday]] plus a special entry for [[PublicHolidays]]); these have now been integrated directly into schema.org.

nodes.label: DaySpa

nodes.label: DeactivateAction

nodes.label: DeclarationOfConformity
nodes.description: A Declaration of Conformity (DoC), a formal document issued by a manufacturer declaring that a product meets specific regulatory requirements.

nodes.label: DecontextualizedContent
nodes.description:
Content coded 'missing context' in a [[MediaReview]], considered in the context of how it was published or shared.

For a [[VideoObject]] to be 'missing context': Presenting unaltered video in an inaccurate manner that misrepresents the footage. For example, using incorrect dates or locations, altering the transcript or sharing brief clips from a longer video to mislead viewers. (A video rated 'original' can also be missing context.)

For an [[ImageObject]] to be 'missing context': Presenting unaltered images in an inaccurate manner to misrepresent the image and mislead the viewer. For example, a common tactic is using an unaltered image but saying it came from a different time or place. (An image rated 'original' can also be missing context.)

For an [[ImageObject]] with embedded text to be 'missing context': An unaltered image presented in an inaccurate manner to misrepresent the image and mislead the viewer. For example, a common tactic is using an unaltered image but saying it came from a different time or place. (An 'original' image with inaccurate text would generally fall in this category.)

For an [[AudioObject]] to be 'missing context': Unaltered audio presented in an inaccurate manner that misrepresents it. For example, using incorrect dates or locations, or sharing brief clips from a longer recording to mislead viewers. (Audio rated “original” can also be missing context.)

nodes.label: DefenceEstablishment
nodes.description: A defence establishment, such as an army or navy base.

nodes.label: DefinedRegion
nodes.description:
A DefinedRegion is a geographic area defined by potentially arbitrary (rather than political, administrative or natural geographical) criteria. Properties are provided for defining a region by reference to sets of postal codes.

Examples: a delivery destination when shopping. Region where regional pricing is configured.

Requirement 1:
Country: US
States: "NY", "CA"

Requirement 2:
Country: US
PostalCode Set: { [94000-94585], [97000, 97999], [13000, 13599]}
{ [12345, 12345], [78945, 78945], }
Region = state, canton, prefecture, autonomous community...

nodes.label: DefinedTerm
nodes.description: A word, name, acronym, phrase, etc. with a formal definition. Often used in the context of category or subject classification, glossaries or dictionaries, product or creative work types, etc. Use the name property for the term being defined, use termCode if the term has an alpha-numeric code allocated, use description to provide the definition of the term. Use the about property to specify what the term is about.

nodes.label: DefinedTermSet
nodes.description: A set of defined terms, for example a set of categories or a classification scheme, a glossary, dictionary or enumeration. Use the about property to specify what the term set is about.

nodes.label: DefinitiveLegalValue
nodes.description:
Indicates a document for which the text is conclusively what the law says and is legally binding. (e.g. The digitally signed version of an Official Journal.)
  Something "Definitive" is considered to be also [[AuthoritativeLegalValue]].

nodes.label: DeleteAction

nodes.label: DeliveryChargeSpecification

nodes.label: DeliveryEvent

nodes.label: DeliveryMethod

Delivery methods are characterized by the means of transportation used, and by the organization or group that is the contracting party for the sending organization or person.

Commonly used values:

* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#DeliveryModeDirectDownload
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#DeliveryModeFreight
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#DeliveryModeMail
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#DeliveryModeOwnFleet
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#DeliveryModePickUp
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#DHL
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#FederalExpress
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#UPS

nodes.label: DeliveryTimeSettings
nodes.description: A DeliveryTimeSettings represents re-usable pieces of shipping information, relating to timing. It is designed for publication on an URL that may be referenced via the [[shippingSettingsLink]] property of an [[OfferShippingDetails]]. Several occurrences can be published, distinguished (and identified/referenced) by their different values for [[transitTimeLabel]].

nodes.label: Demand
nodes.description: A demand entity represents the public, not necessarily binding, not necessarily exclusive, announcement by an organization or person to seek a certain type of goods or services. For describing demand using this type, the very same properties used for Offer apply.

nodes.label: DemoAlbum
nodes.description: DemoAlbum.

nodes.label: DemoGameAvailability
nodes.description: Indicates demo game availability, i.e. a somehow limited demonstration of the full game.

nodes.label: Dentist

nodes.label: Dentistry

nodes.label: DepartAction

nodes.label: DepartmentStore

nodes.label: DepositAccount

nodes.label: Dermatologic

nodes.label: Dermatology
nodes.description: A specific branch of medical science that pertains to diagnosis and treatment of disorders of skin.

nodes.label: DesktopWebPlatform

nodes.label: DiabeticDiet

nodes.label: Diagnostic
nodes.description: A medical device used for diagnostic purposes.

nodes.label: DiagnosticLab

nodes.label: DiagnosticProcedure
nodes.description: A medical procedure intended primarily for diagnostic, as opposed to therapeutic, purposes.

nodes.label: Diet

nodes.label: DietNutrition
nodes.description: Dietetics and nutrition as a medical specialty.

nodes.label: DietarySupplement
nodes.description: A product taken by mouth that contains a dietary ingredient intended to supplement the diet. Dietary ingredients may include vitamins, minerals, herbs or other botanicals, amino acids, and substances such as enzymes, organ tissues, glandulars and metabolites.

nodes.label: DigitalArtDigitalSource
nodes.description: Content coded as 'digital art' using the IPTC digital source type vocabulary.

nodes.label: DigitalAudioTapeFormat
nodes.description: DigitalAudioTapeFormat.

nodes.label: DigitalCaptureDigitalSource
nodes.description: Content coded as 'digital capture' using the IPTC digital source type vocabulary.

nodes.label: DigitalDocument
nodes.description: An electronic file or document.

nodes.label: DigitalDocumentPermission
nodes.description: A permission for a particular person or group to access a particular file.

nodes.label: DigitalDocumentPermissionType
nodes.description: A type of permission which can be granted for accessing a digital document.

nodes.label: DigitalFormat
nodes.description: DigitalFormat.

nodes.label: DigitalPlatformEnumeration
nodes.description: Enumerates some common technology platforms, for use with properties such as [[actionPlatform]]. It is not supposed to be comprehensive - when a suitable code is not enumerated here, textual or URL values can be used instead. These codes are at a fairly high level and do not deal with versioning and other nuance. Additional codes can be suggested [in github](https://github.com/schemaorg/schemaorg/issues/3057).

nodes.label: DigitalProductPassport
nodes.description: A digital product passport (DPP), a record containing information about a product's lifecycle, sustainability, and compliance.

nodes.label: DirectDebit

nodes.label: DisabilitySupport
nodes.description: DisabilitySupport: this is a benefit for disability support.

nodes.label: DisagreeAction

nodes.label: Discontinued
nodes.description: Indicates that the item has been discontinued.

nodes.label: DiscoverAction
nodes.description: The act of discovering/finding an object.

nodes.label: DiscussionForumPosting
nodes.description: A posting to a discussion forum.

nodes.label: DislikeAction
nodes.description: The act of expressing a negative sentiment about the object. An agent dislikes an object (a proposition, topic or theme) with participants.

nodes.label: Distance
nodes.description: Properties that take Distances as values are of the form '<Number> <Length unit of measure>'. E.g., '7 ft'.

nodes.label: DistanceFee
nodes.description: Represents the distance fee (e.g., price per km or mile) part of the total price for an offered product, for example a car rental.

nodes.label: Distillery
nodes.description: A distillery.

nodes.label: DonateAction
nodes.description: The act of providing goods, services, or money without compensation, often for philanthropic reasons.

nodes.label: DoseSchedule
nodes.description: A specific dosing schedule for a drug or supplement.

nodes.label: DoubleBlindedTrial
nodes.description: A trial design in which neither the researcher nor the patient knows the details of the treatment the patient was randomly assigned to.

nodes.label: DownloadAction
nodes.description: The act of downloading an object.

nodes.label: Downpayment
nodes.description: Represents the downpayment (up-front payment) price component of the total price for an offered product that has additional installment payments.

nodes.label: DrawAction
nodes.description: The act of producing a visual/graphical representation of an object, typically with a pen/pencil and paper as instruments.

nodes.label: Drawing
nodes.description: A picture or diagram made with a pencil, pen, or crayon rather than paint.

nodes.label: DrinkAction
nodes.description: The act of swallowing liquids.

nodes.label: DriveWheelConfigurationValue
nodes.description: A value indicating which roadwheels will receive torque.

nodes.label: DrivingSchoolVehicleUsage
nodes.description: Indicates the usage of the vehicle for driving school.

nodes.label: Drug
nodes.description: A chemical or biologic substance, used as a medical therapy, that has a physiological effect on an organism. Here the term drug is used interchangeably with the term medicine although clinical knowledge makes a clear difference between them.

nodes.label: DrugClass
nodes.description: A class of medical drugs, e.g., statins. Classes can represent general pharmacological class, common mechanisms of action, common physiological effects, etc.

nodes.label: DrugCost
nodes.description: The cost per unit of a medical drug. Note that this type is not meant to represent the price in an offer of a drug for sale; see the Offer type for that. This type will typically be used to tag wholesale or average retail cost of a drug, or maximum reimbursable cost. Costs of medical drugs vary widely depending on how and where they are paid for, so while this type captures some of the variables, costs should be used with caution by consumers of this schema's markup.

nodes.label: DrugCostCategory

nodes.label: EditedOrCroppedContent
nodes.description:
Content coded 'edited or cropped content' in a [[MediaReview]], considered in the context of how it was published or shared.

For a [[VideoObject]] to be 'edited or cropped content': The video has been edited or rearranged. This category applies to time edits, including editing multiple videos together to alter the story being told or editing out large portions from a video.

For an [[ImageObject]] to be 'edited or cropped content': Presenting a part of an image from a larger whole to mislead the viewer.

For an [[ImageObject]] with embedded text to be 'edited or cropped content': Presenting a part of an image from a larger whole to mislead the viewer.

For an [[AudioObject]] to be 'edited or cropped content': The audio has been edited or rearranged. This category applies to time edits, including editing multiple audio clips together to alter the story being told or editing out large portions from the recording.

nodes.label: EducationEvent

nodes.label: EducationalAudience

nodes.label: EducationalOccupationalCredential

nodes.label: EducationalOccupationalProgram
nodes.description: A program offered by an institution which determines the learning progress to achieve an outcome, usually a credential like a degree or certificate. This would define a discrete set of opportunities (e.g., job, courses) that together constitute a program with a clear start, end, set of requirements, and transition to a new occupational opportunity (e.g., a job), or sometimes a higher educational opportunity (e.g., an advanced degree).

nodes.label: Emergency

nodes.label: EmergencyService
nodes.description: An emergency service, such as a fire station or ER.

nodes.label: EmployeeRole
nodes.description: A subclass of OrganizationRole used to describe employee relationships.

nodes.label: EmployerAggregateRating
nodes.description: An aggregate rating of an Organization related to its role as an employer.

nodes.label: EmployerReview
nodes.description: An [[EmployerReview]] is a review of an [[Organization]] regarding its role as an employer, written by a current or former employee of that organization.

nodes.label: EmploymentAgency
nodes.description: An employment agency.

nodes.label: Endocrine
nodes.description: A specific branch of medical science that pertains to diagnosis and treatment of disorders of endocrine glands and their secretions.

nodes.label: EndorseAction
nodes.description: An agent approves/certifies/likes/supports/sanctions an object.

nodes.label: EndorsementRating
nodes.description:
An EndorsementRating is a rating that expresses some level of endorsement, for example inclusion in a "critic's pick" blog, a
"Like" or "+1" on a social network. It can be considered the [[result]] of an [[EndorseAction]] in which the [[object]] of the action is rated positively by
some [[agent]]. As is common elsewhere in schema.org, it is sometimes more useful to describe the results of such an action without explicitly describing the [[Action]].

An [[EndorsementRating]] may be part of a numeric scale or organized system, but this is not required: having an explicit type for indicating a positive,
endorsement rating is particularly useful in the absence of numeric scales as it helps consumers understand that the rating is broadly positive.

nodes.label: Energy
nodes.description: Properties that take Energy as values are of the form '<Number> <Energy unit of measure>'.

nodes.label: EnergyConsumptionDetails
nodes.description: EnergyConsumptionDetails represents information related to the energy efficiency of a product that consumes energy. The information that can be provided is based on international regulations such as for example [EU directive 2017/1369](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2017/1369/oj) for energy labeling and the [Energy labeling rule](https://www.ftc.gov/enforcement/rules/rulemaking-regulatory-reform-proceedings/energy-water-use-labeling-consumer) under the Energy Policy and Conservation Act (EPCA) in the US.

nodes.label: EnergyEfficiencyEnumeration
nodes.description: Enumerates energy efficiency levels (also known as "classes" or "ratings") and certifications that are part of several international energy efficiency standards.

nodes.label: EnergyStarCertified
nodes.description: Represents EnergyStar certification.

nodes.label: EnergyStarEnergyEfficiencyEnumeration
nodes.description: Used to indicate whether a product is EnergyStar certified.

nodes.label: EngineSpecification
nodes.description: Information about the engine of the vehicle. A vehicle can have multiple engines represented by multiple engine specification entities.

nodes.label: EnrollingByInvitation
nodes.description: Enrolling participants by invitation only.

nodes.label: EntertainmentBusiness
nodes.description: A business providing entertainment.

nodes.label: EntryPoint
nodes.description: An entry point, within some Web-based protocol.

nodes.label: Enumeration
nodes.description: Lists or enumerations—for example, a list of cuisines or music genres, etc.

nodes.label: EnvironmentalProductDeclaration
nodes.description: An Environmental Product Declaration (EPD) that quantifies environmental information on the life cycle of a product.

nodes.label: Episode
nodes.description: A media episode (e.g. TV, radio, video game) which can be part of a series or season.

nodes.label: Error
nodes.description: Representation of an Error.

nodes.label: Event
nodes.description: An event happening at a certain time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Ticketing information may be added via the [[offers]] property. Repeated events may be structured as separate Event objects.

nodes.label: EventAttendanceModeEnumeration
nodes.description: An EventAttendanceModeEnumeration value is one of potentially several modes of organising an event, relating to whether it is online or offline.

nodes.label: EventCancelled
nodes.description: The event has been cancelled. If the event has multiple startDate values, all are assumed to be cancelled. Either startDate or previousStartDate may be used to specify the event's cancelled date(s).

nodes.label: EventMovedOnline
nodes.description: Indicates that the event was changed to allow online participation. See [[eventAttendanceMode]] for specifics of whether it is now fully or partially online.

nodes.label: EventPostponed
nodes.description: The event has been postponed and no new date has been set. The event's previousStartDate should be set.

nodes.label: EventRescheduled
nodes.description: The event has been rescheduled. The event's previousStartDate should be set to the old date and the startDate should be set to the event's new date. (If the event has been rescheduled multiple times, the previousStartDate property may be repeated.)

nodes.label: EventReservation
nodes.description: A reservation for an event like a concert, sporting event, or lecture.\n\nNote: This type is for information about actual reservations, e.g. in confirmation emails or HTML pages with individual confirmations of reservations. For offers of tickets, use [[Offer]].

nodes.label: EventScheduled
nodes.description: The event is taking place or has taken place on the startDate as scheduled. Use of this value is optional, as it is assumed by default.

nodes.label: EventSeries
nodes.description:
A series of [[Event]]s. Included events can relate with the series using the [[superEvent]] property.

An EventSeries is a collection of events that share some unifying characteristic. For example, "The Olympic Games" is a series, which
is repeated regularly. The "2012 London Olympics" can be presented both as an [[Event]] in the series "Olympic Games", and as an
[[EventSeries]] that included a number of sporting competitions as Events.

The nature of the association between the events in an [[EventSeries]] can vary, but typical examples could
include a thematic event series (e.g. topical meetups or classes), or a series of regular events that share a location, attendee group and/or organizers.

EventSeries has been defined as a kind of Event to make it easy for publishers to use it in an Event context without
worrying about which kinds of series are really event-like enough to call an Event. In general an EventSeries
may seem more Event-like when the period of time is compact and when aspects such as location are fixed, but
it may also sometimes prove useful to describe a longer-term series as an Event.

nodes.label: EventStatusType
nodes.description: EventStatusType is an enumeration type whose instances represent several states that an Event may be in.

nodes.label: EventVenue
nodes.description: An event venue.

nodes.label: EvidenceLevelA
nodes.description: Data derived from multiple randomized clinical trials or meta-analyses.

nodes.label: EvidenceLevelB
nodes.description: Data derived from a single randomized trial, or nonrandomized studies.

nodes.label: EvidenceLevelC
nodes.description: Only consensus opinion of experts, case studies, or standard-of-care.

nodes.label: ExampleMeasurementMethodEnum
nodes.description: An example [[MeasurementMethodEnum]] (to remove when real enums are added).

nodes.label: ExchangeRateSpecification
nodes.description: A structured value representing exchange rate.

nodes.label: ExchangeRefund
nodes.description: Specifies that a refund can be done as an exchange for the same product.

nodes.label: ExerciseAction
nodes.description: The act of participating in exertive activity for the purposes of improving health and fitness.

nodes.label: ExercisePlan

nodes.label: ExhibitionEvent

nodes.label: Eye

nodes.label: FAQPage
nodes.description: A [[FAQPage]] is a [[WebPage]] presenting one or more "[Frequently asked questions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FAQ)" (see also [[QAPage]]).

nodes.label: FDAcategoryA
nodes.description: A designation by the US FDA signifying that adequate and well-controlled studies have failed to demonstrate a risk to the fetus in the first trimester of pregnancy (and there is no evidence of risk in later trimesters).

nodes.label: FDAcategoryB
nodes.description: A designation by the US FDA signifying that animal reproduction studies have failed to demonstrate a risk to the fetus and there are no adequate and well-controlled studies in pregnant women.

nodes.label: FDAcategoryC
nodes.description: A designation by the US FDA signifying that animal reproduction studies have shown an adverse effect on the fetus and there are no adequate and well-controlled studies in humans, but potential benefits may warrant use of the drug in pregnant women despite potential risks.

nodes.label: FDAcategoryD
nodes.description: A designation by the US FDA signifying that there is positive evidence of human fetal risk based on adverse reaction data from investigational or marketing experience or studies in humans, but potential benefits may warrant use of the drug in pregnant women despite potential risks.

nodes.label: FDAcategoryX
nodes.description: A designation by the US FDA signifying that studies in animals or humans have demonstrated fetal abnormalities and/or there is positive evidence of human fetal risk based on adverse reaction data from investigational or marketing experience, and the risks involved in use of the drug in pregnant women clearly outweigh potential benefits.

nodes.label: FDAnotEvaluated
nodes.description: A designation that the drug in question has not been assigned a pregnancy category designation by the US FDA.

nodes.label: FMRadioChannel
nodes.description: A radio channel that uses FM.

nodes.label: FailedActionStatus
nodes.description: An action that failed to complete. The action's error property and the HTTP return code contain more information about the failure.

nodes.label: False
nodes.description: The boolean value false.

nodes.label: FastFoodRestaurant
nodes.description: A fast-food restaurant.

nodes.label: Female

nodes.label: Festival
nodes.description: Event type: Festival.

nodes.label: FilmAction
nodes.description: The act of capturing sound and moving images on film, video, or digitally.

nodes.label: FinancialIncentive
nodes.description:
Represents financial incentives for goods/services offered by an organization (or individual).

Typically contains the [[name]] of the incentive, the [[incentivizedItem]], the [[incentiveAmount]], the [[incentiveStatus]], [[incentiveType]], the [[provider]] of the incentive, and [[eligibleWithSupplier]].

Optionally contains criteria on whether the incentive is limited based on [[purchaseType]], [[purchasePriceLimit]], [[incomeLimit]], and the [[qualifiedExpense]].

nodes.label: FinancialProduct
nodes.description: A product provided to consumers and businesses by financial institutions such as banks, insurance companies, brokerage firms, consumer finance companies, and investment companies which comprise the financial services industry.

nodes.label: FinancialService
nodes.description: Financial services business.

nodes.label: Flight

nodes.label: FlightReservation
nodes.description: A reservation for air travel.\n\nNote: This type is for information about actual reservations, e.g. in confirmation emails or HTML pages with individual confirmations of reservations. For offers of tickets, use [[Offer]].

nodes.label: Float
nodes.description: Data type: Floating number.

nodes.label: FloorPlan
nodes.description: A FloorPlan is an explicit representation of a collection of similar accommodations, allowing the provision of common information (room counts, sizes, layout diagrams) and offers for rental or sale. In typical use, some [[ApartmentComplex]] has an [[accommodationFloorPlan]] which is a [[FloorPlan]].  A FloorPlan is always in the context of a particular place, either a larger [[ApartmentComplex]] or a single [[Apartment]]. The visual/spatial aspects of a floor plan (i.e. room layout, [see wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Floor_plan)) can be indicated using [[image]].

nodes.label: Florist
nodes.description: A florist.

nodes.label: FollowAction
nodes.description:
The act of forming a personal connection with someone/something (object) unidirectionally/asymmetrically to get updates polled from.

Related actions:

* [[BefriendAction]]: Unlike BefriendAction, FollowAction implies that the connection is *not* necessarily reciprocal.
* [[SubscribeAction]]: Unlike SubscribeAction, FollowAction implies that the follower acts as an active agent constantly/actively polling for updates.
* [[RegisterAction]]: Unlike RegisterAction, FollowAction implies that the agent is interested in continuing receiving updates from the object.
* [[JoinAction]]: Unlike JoinAction, FollowAction implies that the agent is interested in getting updates from the object.
* [[TrackAction]]: Unlike TrackAction, FollowAction refers to the polling of updates of all aspects of animate objects rather than the location of inanimate objects (e.g. you track a package, but you don't follow it).

nodes.label: FoodEstablishment
nodes.description: A food-related business.

nodes.label: FoodEstablishmentReservation
nodes.description: A reservation to dine at a food-related business.\n\nNote: This type is for information about actual reservations, e.g. in confirmation emails or HTML pages with individual confirmations of reservations.

nodes.label: FoodEvent
nodes.description: Event type: Food event.

nodes.label: FoodService
nodes.description: A food service, like breakfast, lunch, or dinner.

nodes.label: FourWheelDriveConfiguration
nodes.description: Four-wheel drive is a transmission layout where the engine primarily drives two wheels with a part-time four-wheel drive capability.

nodes.label: FreeReturn

nodes.label: Friday
nodes.description: The day of the week between Thursday and Saturday.

nodes.label: FrontWheelDriveConfiguration
nodes.description: Front-wheel drive is a transmission layout where the engine drives the front wheels.

nodes.description: A type of product fulfillment.

nodes.label: FundingAgency
nodes.description:
A FundingAgency is an organization that implements one or more [[FundingScheme]]s and manages
    the granting process (via [[Grant]]s, typically [[MonetaryGrant]]s).
    A funding agency is not always required for grant funding, e.g. philanthropic giving, corporate sponsorship etc.
    
Examples of funding agencies include ERC, REA, NIH, Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation, ...

nodes.label: FundingScheme
nodes.description:
A FundingScheme combines organizational, project and policy aspects of grant-based funding
    that sets guidelines, principles and mechanisms to support other kinds of projects and activities.
    Funding is typically organized via [[Grant]] funding. Examples of funding schemes: Swiss Priority Programmes (SPPs); EU Framework 7 (FP7); Horizon 2020; the NIH-R01 Grant Program; Wellcome institutional strategic support fund. For large scale public sector funding, the management and administration of grant awards is often handled by other, dedicated, organizations - [[FundingAgency]]s such as ERC, REA, ...

nodes.label: Fungus
nodes.description: Pathogenic fungus.

nodes.label: FurnitureStore
nodes.description: A furniture store.

nodes.label: Game
nodes.description: The Game type represents things which are games. These are typically rule-governed recreational activities, e.g. role-playing games in which players assume the role of characters in a fictional setting.

nodes.label: GameAvailabilityEnumeration
nodes.description: For a [[VideoGame]], such as used with a [[PlayGameAction]], an enumeration of the kind of game availability offered.

nodes.label: GamePlayMode
nodes.description: Indicates whether this game is multi-player, co-op or single-player.

nodes.label: GameServer
nodes.description: Server that provides game interaction in a multiplayer game.

nodes.label: GameServerStatus
nodes.description: Status of a game server.

nodes.description: A garden store.

nodes.label: GasStation
nodes.description: A gas station.

nodes.description: A specific branch of medical science that pertains to diagnosis and treatment of disorders of digestive system.

nodes.description: Residence type: Gated community.

nodes.label: GeneralContractor
nodes.description: A general contractor.

nodes.label: GenericWebPlatform
nodes.description: Represents the generic notion of the Web Platform. More specific codes include [[MobileWebPlatform]] and [[DesktopWebPlatform]], as an incomplete list.

nodes.label: Genetic
nodes.description: A specific branch of medical science that pertains to hereditary transmission and the variation of inherited characteristics and disorders.

nodes.label: Genitourinary
nodes.description: Genitourinary system function assessment with clinical examination.

nodes.label: GeoCircle
nodes.description:
A GeoCircle is a GeoShape representing a circular geographic area. As it is a GeoShape
          it provides the simple textual property 'circle', but also allows the combination of postalCode alongside geoRadius.
          The center of the circle can be indicated via the 'geoMidpoint' property, or more approximately using 'address', 'postalCode'.

nodes.label: GeoCoordinates
nodes.description: The geographic coordinates of a place or event.

nodes.label: GeoShape
nodes.description: The geographic shape of a place. A GeoShape can be described using several properties whose values are based on latitude/longitude pairs. Either whitespace or commas can be used to separate latitude and longitude; whitespace should be used when writing a list of several such points.

nodes.label: GeospatialGeometry
nodes.description: (Eventually to be defined as) a supertype of GeoShape designed to accommodate definitions from Geo-Spatial best practices.

nodes.label: Geriatric

nodes.label: GettingAccessHealthAspect

nodes.label: GiveAction

The act of transferring ownership of an object to a destination. Reciprocal of TakeAction.

Related actions:

* [[TakeAction]]: Reciprocal of GiveAction.
* [[SendAction]]: Unlike SendAction, GiveAction implies that ownership is being transferred (e.g. I may send my laptop to you, but that doesn't mean I'm giving it to you).

nodes.label: GlutenFreeDiet
nodes.description: A diet exclusive of gluten.

nodes.label: GolfCourse

nodes.label: GovernmentBenefitsType
nodes.description: GovernmentBenefitsType enumerates several kinds of government benefits to support the COVID-19 situation. Note that this structure may not capture all benefits offered.

nodes.label: GovernmentBuilding
nodes.description: A government building.

nodes.label: GovernmentOffice
nodes.description: A government office—for example, an IRS or DMV office.

nodes.label: GovernmentOrganization
nodes.description: A governmental organization or agency.

nodes.label: GovernmentPermit
nodes.description: A permit issued by a government agency.

nodes.label: GovernmentService
nodes.description: A service provided by a government organization, e.g. food stamps, veterans benefits, etc.

nodes.label: Grant
nodes.description:
A grant, typically financial or otherwise quantifiable, of resources. Typically a [[funder]] sponsors some [[MonetaryAmount]] to an [[Organization]] or [[Person]],
    sometimes not necessarily via a dedicated or long-lived [[Project]], resulting in one or more outputs, or [[fundedItem]]s. For financial sponsorship, indicate the [[funder]] of a [[MonetaryGrant]]. For non-financial support, indicate [[sponsor]] of [[Grant]]s of resources (e.g. office space).

Grants support  activities directed towards some agreed collective goals, often but not always organized as [[Project]]s. Long-lived projects are sometimes sponsored by a variety of grants over time, but it is also common for a project to be associated with a single grant.

The amount of a [[Grant]] is represented using [[amount]] as a [[MonetaryAmount]].

nodes.label: GraphicNovel
nodes.description:
This type is deprecated: GraphicNovel does not fit the BookFormatType enumeration, as it can appear in multiple formats (e.g., Hardcover, eBook). It is not mutually exclusive and therefore deprecated. Use standard BookFormatType values instead in combination with the SequentialArt.

Book format: GraphicNovel. May represent a bound collection of ComicIssue instances.

nodes.label: GroceryStore

nodes.label: GroupBoardingPolicy

A [[Guide]] may represent a Buying Guide and detail aspects of products or services for a user to consider. A [[Guide]] may represent a Product Guide and recommend specific products or services. A [[Guide]] may represent a Ranked List and recommend specific products or services with ranking.

nodes.label: Gynecologic

nodes.label: HVACBusiness

nodes.label: Hackathon
nodes.description: A [hackathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hackathon) event.

nodes.label: HairSalon

nodes.label: HalalDiet

nodes.label: Hardcover

nodes.label: HardwareStore

nodes.label: Head

nodes.label: HealthAndBeautyBusiness

nodes.label: HealthCare

nodes.label: HealthClub

nodes.label: HealthcareConsideration

nodes.label: HearingImpairedSupported

nodes.label: Hematologic

nodes.label: HinduDiet

nodes.label: HinduTemple

nodes.label: HobbyShop

nodes.label: HomeAndConstructionBusiness

A construction business.

As a [[LocalBusiness]] it can be described as a [[provider]] of one or more [[Service]]\(s).

nodes.label: HomeGoodsStore

nodes.label: Homeopathic

nodes.label: Hospital

nodes.label: Hostel

A hostel - cheap accommodation, often in shared dormitories.
