nodes.label: Hotel
nodes.description:
A hotel is an establishment that provides lodging paid on a short-term basis (source: Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia, see http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hotel).

See also the dedicated document on the use of schema.org for marking up hotels and other forms of accommodations.

nodes.label: HotelRoom
nodes.description:
A hotel room is a single room in a hotel.

See also the dedicated document on the use of schema.org for marking up hotels and other forms of accommodations.

nodes.label: House
nodes.description: A house is a building or structure that has the ability to be occupied for habitation by humans or other creatures (source: Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia, see http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House).

nodes.label: HousePainter
nodes.description: A house painting service.

nodes.label: HowItWorksHealthAspect
nodes.description: Content that discusses and explains how a particular health-related topic works, e.g. in terms of mechanisms and underlying science.

nodes.label: HowOrWhereHealthAspect
nodes.description: Information about how or where to find a topic. Also may contain location data that can be used for where to look for help if the topic is observed.

nodes.label: HowTo
nodes.description: Instructions that explain how to achieve a result by performing a sequence of steps.

nodes.label: HowToDirection
nodes.description: A direction indicating a single action to do in the instructions for how to achieve a result.

nodes.label: HowToItem
nodes.description: An item used as either a tool or supply when performing the instructions for how to achieve a result.

nodes.label: HowToSection
nodes.description: A sub-grouping of steps in the instructions for how to achieve a result (e.g. steps for making a pie crust within a pie recipe).

nodes.label: HowToStep
nodes.description: A step in the instructions for how to achieve a result. It is an ordered list with HowToDirection and/or HowToTip items.

nodes.label: HowToSupply
nodes.description: A supply consumed when performing the instructions for how to achieve a result.

nodes.label: HowToTip
nodes.description: An explanation in the instructions for how to achieve a result. It provides supplementary information about a technique, supply, author's preference, etc. It can explain what could be done, or what should not be done, but doesn't specify what should be done (see HowToDirection).

nodes.label: HowToTool
nodes.description: A tool used (but not consumed) when performing instructions for how to achieve a result.

nodes.label: HyperToc
nodes.description: A HyperToc represents a hypertext table of contents for complex media objects, such as [[VideoObject]], [[AudioObject]]. Items in the table of contents are indicated using the [[tocEntry]] property, and typed [[HyperTocEntry]]. For cases where the same larger work is split into multiple files, [[associatedMedia]] can be used on individual [[HyperTocEntry]] items.

nodes.label: HyperTocEntry
nodes.description: A HyperToEntry is an item within a [[HyperToc]], which represents a hypertext table of contents for complex media objects, such as [[VideoObject]], [[AudioObject]]. The media object itself is indicated using [[associatedMedia]]. Each section of interest within that content can be described with a [[HyperTocEntry]], with associated [[startOffset]] and [[endOffset]]. When several entries are all from the same file, [[associatedMedia]] is used on the overarching [[HyperTocEntry]]; if the content has been split into multiple files, they can be referenced using [[associatedMedia]] on each [[HyperTocEntry]].

nodes.label: IOSPlatform
nodes.description: Represents the broad notion of iOS-based operating systems.

nodes.label: IPTCDigitalSourceEnumeration
nodes.description: IPTC "Digital Source" codes for use with the [[digitalSourceType]] property, providing information about the source for a digital media object. In general these codes are not declared here to be mutually exclusive, although some combinations would be contradictory if applied simultaneously, or might be considered mutually incompatible by upstream maintainers of the definitions. See the IPTC documentation for detailed definitions of all terms.

nodes.label: ITAmateurSportsClubCharity
nodes.description: ITAmateurSportsClubCharity: Non-profit type referring to Italian amateur sports clubs organized in corporate form (Ital. società sportiva dilettantistica or SSD), as distinct from amateur sports associations (Ital. associazione sportiva dilettantistica or ASD), governed primarily by Legislative Decree No. 36 of 28 February 2021, as amended, and registered in the national register of amateur sports activities established by Legislative Decree No. 39 of 28 February 2021. These entities are generally outside the Italian Third Sector unless also registered in the RUNTS.

nodes.label: ITAssociativeNetworkCharity
nodes.description: ITAssociativeNetworkCharity: Non-profit type referring to Italian associative networks (Ital. rete associativa), associations grouping a large number of Third Sector entities, governed by Article 41 and related provisions of Legislative Decree No. 117 of 3 July 2017, the Italian Third Sector Code.

nodes.label: ITCooperativeCharity
nodes.description: ITCooperativeCharity: Non-profit type referring to Italian social cooperatives (Ital. cooperativa sociale), governed primarily by Law 381 of 8 November 1991. Social cooperatives and their consortia qualify as social enterprises by operation of law under Article 1(4) of Legislative Decree No. 112 of 3 July 2017.

nodes.label: ITMutualAidCharity
nodes.description: ITMutualAidCharity: Non-profit type referring to Italian mutual aid societies (Ital. società di mutuo soccorso or SOMS), governed by Law 3818 of 15 April 1886, in coordination with Articles 42 and following of Legislative Decree No. 117 of 3 July 2017, the Italian Third Sector Code.

nodes.label: ITNonprofitType
nodes.description: ITNonprofitType: Non-profit organization type originating from Italy. Most categories are drawn from the Italian Third Sector Code (Legislative Decree No. 117 of 3 July 2017), although some Italian non-profit entities, such as amateur sports entities, are primarily governed by other legislation.

nodes.label: ITOtherThirdSectorEntityCharity
nodes.description: ITOtherThirdSectorEntityCharity: Non-profit type referring to other Italian Third Sector entities (Ital. Ente del Terzo settore or ETS) registered in the Registro unico nazionale del Terzo settore (RUNTS) under Article 4 of Legislative Decree No. 117 of 3 July 2017 that do not fall within one of the specifically enumerated Third Sector categories.

nodes.label: ITPhilanthropicEntityCharity
nodes.description: ITPhilanthropicEntityCharity: Non-profit type referring to Italian philanthropic entities (Ital. ente filantropico), constituted as recognized associations or foundations and governed by Articles 37 and following of Legislative Decree No. 117 of 3 July 2017, the Italian Third Sector Code.

nodes.label: ITSocialCompanyCharity
nodes.description: ITSocialCompanyCharity: Non-profit type referring to Italian social enterprises (Ital. impresa sociale), a status governed by Legislative Decree No. 112 of 3 July 2017, as amended. The status may be acquired by different types of private entities and is not limited to companies.

nodes.label: ITSocialCooperativeCharity
nodes.description: ITSocialCooperativeCharity: Non-profit type referring to Italian social cooperatives (Ital. cooperativa sociale), governed primarily by Law 381 of 8 November 1991. Social cooperatives and their consortia qualify as social enterprises by operation of law under Article 1(4) of Legislative Decree No. 112 of 3 July 2017.

nodes.label: ITSocialEnterpriseCharity
nodes.description: ITSocialEnterpriseCharity: Non-profit type referring to Italian social enterprises (Ital. impresa sociale), a status governed by Legislative Decree No. 112 of 3 July 2017, as amended. The status may be acquired by different types of private entities and is not limited to companies.

nodes.label: ITSocialPromotionCharity
nodes.description: ITSocialPromotionCharity: Non-profit type referring to Italian social promotion associations (Ital. associazione di promozione sociale or APS), governed primarily by Articles 35 and following of Legislative Decree No. 117 of 3 July 2017, the Italian Third Sector Code, which superseded Law 383 of 2000.

nodes.label: ITSportCompanyCharity
nodes.description: ITSportCompanyCharity: Non-profit type referring to Italian amateur sports clubs organized in corporate form (Ital. società sportiva dilettantistica or SSD), as distinct from amateur sports associations (Ital. associazione sportiva dilettantistica or ASD), governed primarily by Legislative Decree No. 36 of 28 February 2021, as amended, and registered in the national register of amateur sports activities established by Legislative Decree No. 39 of 28 February 2021. These entities are generally outside the Italian Third Sector unless also registered in the RUNTS.

nodes.label: ITVolunteerAssociationCharity
nodes.description: ITVolunteerAssociationCharity: Non-profit type referring to Italian volunteer organizations (Ital. organizzazione di volontariato or ODV), governed primarily by Articles 32 and following of Legislative Decree No. 117 of 3 July 2017, the Italian Third Sector Code, which superseded Law 266 of 1991.

nodes.label: IceCreamShop
nodes.description: An ice cream shop.

nodes.label: IgnoreAction
nodes.description: The act of intentionally disregarding the object. An agent ignores an object.

nodes.label: ImageGallery
nodes.description: Web page type: Image gallery page.

nodes.label: ImageObject
nodes.description: An image file.

nodes.label: ImageObjectSnapshot
nodes.description: A specific and exact (byte-for-byte) version of an [[ImageObject]]. Two byte-for-byte identical files, for the purposes of this type, considered identical. If they have different embedded metadata (e.g. XMP, EXIF) the files will differ. Different external facts about the files, e.g. creator or dateCreated that aren't represented in their actual content, do not affect this notion of identity.

nodes.label: ImagingTest
nodes.description: Any medical imaging modality typically used for diagnostic purposes.

nodes.label: InForce
nodes.description: Indicates that a legislation is in force.

nodes.label: InStock
nodes.description: Indicates that the item is in stock.

nodes.label: InStoreOnly
nodes.description: Indicates that the item is available only at physical locations.

nodes.label: InStorePrepay
nodes.description: Payment in advance in some form of shop or kiosk for goods purchased online.

nodes.label: IncentiveQualifiedExpenseType
nodes.description: The types of expenses that are covered by the incentive. For example some incentives are only for the goods (tangible items) but the services (labor) are excluded.

nodes.label: IncentiveQualifiedExpenseTypeGoodsOnly
nodes.description: This incentive applies to goods only.

nodes.label: IncentiveQualifiedExpenseTypeGoodsOrServices
nodes.description: This incentive can apply to either goods or services (or both).

nodes.label: IncentiveQualifiedExpenseTypeServicesOnly
nodes.description: This incentive applies to services only.

nodes.label: IncentiveQualifiedExpenseTypeUtilityBill
nodes.description: This incentive applies to utility bills.

nodes.label: IncentiveStatus
nodes.description: Enumerates a status for an incentive, such as whether it is active.

nodes.label: IncentiveStatusActive
nodes.description: This incentive is currently active.

nodes.label: IncentiveStatusInDevelopment
nodes.description: This incentive is currently being developed, and may become active/retired in the future.

nodes.label: IncentiveStatusOnHold
nodes.description: This incentive is currently active, but may not be accepting new applicants (e.g. max number of redemptions reached for a year)

nodes.label: IncentiveStatusRetired
nodes.description: This incentive is not longer available.

nodes.label: IncentiveType
nodes.description: Enumerates common financial incentives for products, including tax credits, tax deductions, rebates and subsidies, etc.

nodes.label: IncentiveTypeLoan
nodes.description: An incentive where the recipient can receive additional funding for the purchase/lease of the good/service, which must be paid back.

nodes.label: IncentiveTypeRebateOrSubsidy
nodes.description: An incentive that reduces the purchase/lease cost of the good/service in question.

nodes.label: IncentiveTypeTaxCredit
nodes.description: An incentive that directly reduces the amount of tax owed by the recipient.

nodes.label: IncentiveTypeTaxDeduction
nodes.description: An incentive that reduces the recipient's amount of taxable income.

nodes.label: IncentiveTypeTaxWaiver
nodes.description: An incentive that reduces/exempts the recipient from taxation applicable to the incentivized good/service (e.g. luxury taxes, registration taxes, circulation tax).

nodes.label: IndividualPhysician
nodes.description:
An individual medical practitioner. For their official address use [[address]], for affiliations to hospitals use [[hospitalAffiliation]]. 
The [[practicesAt]] property can be used to indicate [[MedicalOrganization]] hospitals, clinics, pharmacies etc. where this physician practices.

nodes.label: IndividualProduct
nodes.description: A single, identifiable product instance (e.g. a laptop with a particular serial number).

nodes.label: Infectious
nodes.description: Something in medical science that pertains to infectious diseases, i.e. caused by bacterial, viral, fungal or parasitic infections.

nodes.label: InfectiousAgentClass
nodes.description: Classes of agents or pathogens that transmit infectious diseases. Enumerated type.

nodes.label: InfectiousDisease
nodes.description: An infectious disease is a clinically evident human disease resulting from the presence of pathogenic microbial agents, like pathogenic viruses, pathogenic bacteria, fungi, protozoa, multicellular parasites, and prions. To be considered an infectious disease, such pathogens are known to be able to cause this disease.

nodes.label: InformAction
nodes.description: The act of notifying someone of information pertinent to them, with no expectation of a response.

nodes.label: IngredientsHealthAspect
nodes.description: Content discussing ingredients-related aspects of a health topic.

nodes.label: InsertAction
nodes.description: The act of adding at a specific location in an ordered collection.

nodes.label: InstallAction
nodes.description: The act of installing an application.

nodes.label: Installment
nodes.description: Represents the installment pricing component of the total price for an offered product.

nodes.label: InstantaneousEvent
nodes.description: An event with no duration, like for instance a computer log entry.

nodes.label: InsuranceAgency
nodes.description: An Insurance agency.

nodes.label: Intangible
nodes.description: A utility class that serves as the umbrella for a number of 'intangible' things such as quantities, structured values, etc.

nodes.label: Integer
nodes.description: Data type: Integer.

nodes.label: InteractAction
nodes.description: The act of interacting with another person or organization.

nodes.label: InteractionCounter
nodes.description: A summary of how users have interacted with this CreativeWork. In most cases, authors will use a subtype to specify the specific type of interaction.

nodes.label: InternationalTrial
nodes.description: An international trial.

nodes.label: InternetCafe
nodes.description: An internet cafe.

nodes.label: InvestmentFund
nodes.description: A company or fund that gathers capital from a number of investors to create a pool of money that is then re-invested into stocks, bonds and other assets.

nodes.label: InvestmentOrDeposit
nodes.description: A type of financial product that typically requires the client to transfer funds to a financial service in return for potential beneficial financial return.

nodes.label: InviteAction
nodes.description: The act of asking someone to attend an event. Reciprocal of RsvpAction.

nodes.label: Invoice
nodes.description: A statement of the money due for goods or services; a bill.

nodes.label: InvoicePrice
nodes.description: Represents the invoice price of an offered product.

nodes.label: ItemAvailability
nodes.description: A list of possible product availability options.

nodes.label: ItemList
nodes.description: A list of items of any sort—for example, Top 10 Movies About Weathermen, or Top 100 Party Songs. Not to be confused with HTML lists, which are often used only for formatting.

nodes.label: ItemListOrderAscending
nodes.description: An ItemList ordered with lower values listed first.

nodes.label: ItemListOrderDescending
nodes.description: An ItemList ordered with higher values listed first.

nodes.label: ItemListOrderType
nodes.description: Enumerated for values for itemListOrder for indicating how an ordered ItemList is organized.

nodes.label: ItemListUnordered
nodes.description: An ItemList ordered with no explicit order.

nodes.label: ItemPage
nodes.description: A page devoted to a single item, such as a particular product or hotel.

nodes.label: JewelryStore
nodes.description: A jewelry store.

nodes.label: JobPosting
nodes.description: A listing that describes a job opening in a certain organization.

nodes.label: JoinAction
nodes.description:
An agent joins an event/group with participants/friends at a location.

Related actions:

* [[RegisterAction]]: Unlike RegisterAction, JoinAction refers to joining a group/team of people.
* [[SubscribeAction]]: Unlike SubscribeAction, JoinAction does not imply that you'll be receiving updates.
* [[FollowAction]]: Unlike FollowAction, JoinAction does not imply that you'll be polling for updates.

nodes.label: Joint
nodes.description: The anatomical location at which two or more bones make contact.

nodes.label: KeepProduct
nodes.description: Specifies that the consumer can keep the product, even when receiving a refund or store credit.

nodes.label: KosherDiet
nodes.description: A diet conforming to Jewish dietary practices.

nodes.label: LaboratoryScience
nodes.description: A medical science pertaining to chemical, hematological, immunologic, microscopic, or bacteriological diagnostic analyses or research.

nodes.label: LakeBodyOfWater
nodes.description: A lake (for example, Lake Pontrachain).

nodes.label: Landform
nodes.description: A landform or physical feature.  Landform elements include mountains, plains, lakes, rivers, seascape and oceanic waterbody interface features such as bays, peninsulas, seas and so forth, including sub-aqueous terrain features such as submersed mountain ranges, volcanoes, and the great ocean basins.

nodes.label: LandmarksOrHistoricalBuildings
nodes.description: An historical landmark or building.

nodes.label: Language
nodes.description: Natural languages such as Spanish, Tamil, Hindi, English, etc. Formal language code tags expressed in [BCP 47](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IETF_language_tag) can be used via the [[alternateName]] property. The Language type previously also covered programming languages such as Scheme and Lisp, which are now best represented using [[ComputerLanguage]].

nodes.label: LaserDiscFormat
nodes.description: LaserDiscFormat.

nodes.label: LearningResource
nodes.description:
The LearningResource type can be used to indicate [[CreativeWork]]s (whether physical or digital) that have a particular and explicit orientation towards learning, education, skill acquisition, and other educational purposes.

[[LearningResource]] is expected to be used as an addition to a primary type such as [[Book]], [[VideoObject]], [[Product]] etc.

[[EducationEvent]] serves a similar purpose for event-like things (e.g. a [[Trip]]). A [[LearningResource]] may be created as a result of an [[EducationEvent]], for example by recording one.

nodes.label: LeaveAction
nodes.description:
An agent leaves an event / group with participants/friends at a location.

Related actions:

* [[JoinAction]]: The antonym of LeaveAction.
* [[UnRegisterAction]]: Unlike UnRegisterAction, LeaveAction implies leaving a group/team of people rather than a service.

nodes.label: LeftHandDriving
nodes.description: The steering position is on the left side of the vehicle (viewed from the main direction of driving).

nodes.label: LegalForceStatus
nodes.description: A list of possible statuses for the legal force of a legislation.

nodes.label: LegalService
nodes.description: A LegalService is a business that provides legally-oriented services, advice and representation, e.g. law firms.\n\nAs a [[LocalBusiness]] it can be described as a [[provider]] of one or more [[Service]]\(s).

nodes.label: LegalValueLevel
nodes.description: A list of possible levels for the legal validity of a legislation.

nodes.label: Legislation
nodes.description: A legal document such as an act, decree, bill, etc. (enforceable or not) or a component of a legal act (like an article).

nodes.label: LegislationObject
nodes.description: A specific object or file containing a Legislation. Note that the same Legislation can be published in multiple files. For example, a digitally signed PDF, a plain PDF and an HTML version.

nodes.label: LegislativeBuilding
nodes.description: A legislative building—for example, the state capitol.

nodes.label: LeisureTimeActivity
nodes.description: Any physical activity engaged in for recreational purposes. Examples may include ballroom dancing, roller skating, canoeing, fishing, etc.

nodes.label: LendAction
nodes.description:
The act of providing an object under an agreement that it will be returned at a later date. Reciprocal of BorrowAction.

Related actions:

* [[BorrowAction]]: Reciprocal of LendAction.

nodes.label: Library
nodes.description: A library.

nodes.label: LibrarySystem
nodes.description: A [[LibrarySystem]] is a collaborative system amongst several libraries.

nodes.label: LifestyleModification
nodes.description: A process of care involving exercise, changes to diet, fitness routines, and other lifestyle changes aimed at improving a health condition.

nodes.label: Ligament
nodes.description: A short band of tough, flexible, fibrous connective tissue that functions to connect multiple bones, cartilages, and structurally support joints.

nodes.label: LikeAction
nodes.description: The act of expressing a positive sentiment about the object. An agent likes an object (a proposition, topic or theme) with participants.

nodes.label: LimitedAvailability
nodes.description: Indicates that the item has limited availability.

nodes.label: LimitedByGuaranteeCharity
nodes.description: LimitedByGuaranteeCharity: Non-profit type referring to a charitable company that is limited by guarantee (UK).

nodes.label: LinkRole
nodes.description: A Role that represents a Web link, e.g. as expressed via the 'url' property. Its linkRelationship property can indicate URL-based and plain textual link types, e.g. those in IANA link registry or others such as 'amphtml'. This structure provides a placeholder where details from HTML's link element can be represented outside of HTML, e.g. in JSON-LD feeds.

nodes.label: LiquorStore
nodes.description: A shop that sells alcoholic drinks such as wine, beer, whisky and other spirits.

nodes.label: ListItem
nodes.description: An list item, e.g. a step in a checklist or how-to description.

nodes.label: ListPrice
nodes.description: Represents the list price of an offered product. Typically the same as the [MSRP](https://schema.org/MSRP).

nodes.label: ListenAction
nodes.description: The act of consuming audio content.

nodes.label: LiteraryEvent
nodes.description: Event type: Literary event.

nodes.label: LiveAlbum
nodes.description: LiveAlbum.

nodes.label: LiveBlogPosting
nodes.description: A [[LiveBlogPosting]] is a [[BlogPosting]] intended to provide a rolling textual coverage of an ongoing event through continuous updates.

nodes.label: LivingWithHealthAspect
nodes.description: Information about coping or life related to the topic.

nodes.label: LoanOrCredit
nodes.description: A financial product for the loaning of an amount of money, or line of credit, under agreed terms and charges.

nodes.label: LocalBusiness
nodes.description: A particular physical business or branch of an organization. Examples of LocalBusiness include a restaurant, a particular branch of a restaurant chain, a branch of a bank, a medical practice, a club, a bowling alley, etc.

nodes.label: LocationFeatureSpecification
nodes.description: Specifies a location feature by providing a structured value representing a feature of an accommodation as a property-value pair of varying degrees of formality.

nodes.label: LockerDelivery
nodes.description: A DeliveryMethod in which an item is made available via locker.

nodes.label: Locksmith
nodes.description: A locksmith.

nodes.label: LodgingBusiness
nodes.description: A lodging business, such as a motel, hotel, or inn.

nodes.label: LodgingReservation
nodes.description: A reservation for lodging at a hotel, motel, inn, etc.\n\nNote: This type is for information about actual reservations, e.g. in confirmation emails or HTML pages with individual confirmations of reservations.

nodes.label: LoginAction
nodes.description: The action of logging into a device or application.

nodes.label: Longitudinal
nodes.description: Unlike cross-sectional studies, longitudinal studies track the same people, and therefore the differences observed in those people are less likely to be the result of cultural differences across generations. Longitudinal studies are also used in medicine to uncover predictors of certain diseases.

nodes.label: LoseAction
nodes.description: The act of being defeated in a competitive activity.

nodes.label: LowCalorieDiet
nodes.description: A diet focused on reduced calorie intake.

nodes.label: LowFatDiet
nodes.description: A diet focused on reduced fat and cholesterol intake.

nodes.label: LowLactoseDiet
nodes.description: A diet appropriate for people with lactose intolerance.

nodes.label: LowSaltDiet
nodes.description: A diet focused on reduced sodium intake.

nodes.label: Lung
nodes.description: Lung and respiratory system clinical examination.

nodes.label: LymphaticVessel
nodes.description: A type of blood vessel that specifically carries lymph fluid unidirectionally toward the heart.

nodes.label: MRI
nodes.description: Magnetic resonance imaging.

nodes.label: MSRP
nodes.description: Represents the manufacturer suggested retail price ("MSRP") of an offered product.

nodes.label: MadeToOrder
nodes.description: Indicates that the item is made to order (custom made).

nodes.label: Male
nodes.description: The male gender.

nodes.label: Manuscript
nodes.description: A book, document, or piece of music written by hand rather than typed or printed.

nodes.label: Map
nodes.description: A map.

nodes.label: MapCategoryType
nodes.description: An enumeration of several kinds of Map.

nodes.label: MarryAction
nodes.description: The act of marrying a person.

nodes.label: Mass
nodes.description: Properties that take Mass as values are of the form '<Number> <Mass unit of measure>'. E.g., '7 kg'.

nodes.label: MathSolver
nodes.description: A math solver which is capable of solving a subset of mathematical problems.

nodes.label: MaximumDoseSchedule
nodes.description: The maximum dosing schedule considered safe for a drug or supplement as recommended by an authority or by the drug/supplement's manufacturer. Capture the recommending authority in the recognizingAuthority property of MedicalEntity.

nodes.label: MaximumRetailPrice
nodes.description: The maximum retail price (MRP) of a product sold in India.

nodes.label: MayTreatHealthAspect
nodes.description: Related topics may be treated by a Topic.

nodes.label: MeasurementMethodEnum
nodes.description: Enumeration(s) for use with [[measurementMethod]].

nodes.label: MeasurementTypeEnumeration
nodes.description: Enumeration of common measurement types (or dimensions), for example "chest" for a person, "inseam" for pants, "gauge" for screws, or "wheel" for bicycles.

nodes.label: MediaEnumeration
nodes.description: MediaEnumeration enumerations are lists of codes, labels etc. useful for describing media objects. They may be reflections of externally developed lists, or created at schema.org, or a combination.

nodes.label: MediaGallery
nodes.description: Web page type: Media gallery page. A mixed-media page that can contain media such as images, videos, and other multimedia.

nodes.label: MediaManipulationRatingEnumeration
nodes.description: Codes for use with the [[mediaAuthenticityCategory]] property, indicating the authenticity of a media object (in the context of how it was published or shared). In general these codes are not mutually exclusive, although some combinations (such as 'original' versus 'transformed', 'edited' and 'staged') would be contradictory if applied in the same [[MediaReview]]. Note that the application of these codes is with regard to a piece of media shared or published in a particular context.

nodes.label: MediaObject
nodes.description: A media object, such as an image, video, audio, or text object embedded in a web page or a downloadable dataset i.e. DataDownload. Note that a creative work may have many media objects associated with it on the same web page. For example, a page about a single song (MusicRecording) may have a music video (VideoObject), and a high and low bandwidth audio stream (2 AudioObject's).

nodes.label: MediaReview
nodes.description:
A [[MediaReview]] is a more specialized form of Review dedicated to the evaluation of media content online, typically in the context of fact-checking and misinformation.
    For more general reviews of media in the broader sense, use [[UserReview]], [[CriticReview]] or other [[Review]] types. This definition is
    a work in progress. While the [[MediaManipulationRatingEnumeration]] list reflects significant community review amongst fact-checkers and others working
    to combat misinformation, the specific structures for representing media objects, their versions and publication context, are still evolving. Similarly, best practices for the relationship between [[MediaReview]] and [[ClaimReview]] markup have not yet been finalized.

nodes.label: MediaReviewItem
nodes.description: Represents an item or group of closely related items treated as a unit for the sake of evaluation in a [[MediaReview]]. Authorship etc. apply to the items rather than to the curation/grouping or reviewing party.

nodes.label: MediaSubscription
nodes.description: A subscription which allows a user to access media including audio, video, books, etc.

nodes.label: MedicalAudience
nodes.description: Target audiences for medical web pages.

nodes.label: MedicalAudienceType
nodes.description: Target audiences types for medical web pages. Enumerated type.

nodes.label: MedicalBusiness
nodes.description: A particular physical or virtual business of an organization for medical purposes. Examples of MedicalBusiness include different businesses run by health professionals.

nodes.label: MedicalCause
nodes.description: The causative agent(s) that are responsible for the pathophysiologic process that eventually results in a medical condition, symptom or sign. In this schema, unless otherwise specified this is meant to be the proximate cause of the medical condition, symptom or sign. The proximate cause is defined as the causative agent that most directly results in the medical condition, symptom or sign. For example, the HIV virus could be considered a cause of AIDS. Or in a diagnostic context, if a patient fell and sustained a hip fracture and two days later sustained a pulmonary embolism which eventuated in a cardiac arrest, the cause of the cardiac arrest (the proximate cause) would be the pulmonary embolism and not the fall. Medical causes can include cardiovascular, chemical, dermatologic, endocrine, environmental, gastroenterologic, genetic, hematologic, gynecologic, iatrogenic, infectious, musculoskeletal, neurologic, nutritional, obstetric, oncologic, otolaryngologic, pharmacologic, psychiatric, pulmonary, renal, rheumatologic, toxic, traumatic, or urologic causes; medical conditions can be causes as well.

nodes.label: MedicalClinic
nodes.description: A facility, often associated with a hospital or medical school, that is devoted to the specific diagnosis and/or healthcare. Previously limited to outpatients but with evolution it may be open to inpatients as well.

nodes.label: MedicalCode
nodes.description: A code for a medical entity.

nodes.label: MedicalCondition
nodes.description: Any condition of the human body that affects the normal functioning of a person, whether physically or mentally. Includes diseases, injuries, disabilities, disorders, syndromes, etc.

nodes.label: MedicalConditionStage
nodes.description: A stage of a medical condition, such as 'Stage IIIa'.

nodes.label: MedicalContraindication
nodes.description: A condition or factor that serves as a reason to withhold a certain medical therapy. Contraindications can be absolute (there are no reasonable circumstances for undertaking a course of action) or relative (the patient is at higher risk of complications, but these risks may be outweighed by other considerations or mitigated by other measures).

nodes.label: MedicalDevice
nodes.description: Any object used in a medical capacity, such as to diagnose or treat a patient.

nodes.label: MedicalDevicePurpose
nodes.description: Categories of medical devices, organized by the purpose or intended use of the device.

nodes.label: MedicalEntity
nodes.description: The most generic type of entity related to health and the practice of medicine.

nodes.label: MedicalEnumeration
nodes.description: Enumerations related to health and the practice of medicine: A concept that is used to attribute a quality to another concept, as a qualifier, a collection of items or a listing of all of the elements of a set in medicine practice.

nodes.label: MedicalEvidenceLevel
nodes.description: Level of evidence for a medical guideline. Enumerated type.

nodes.label: MedicalGuideline
nodes.description: Any recommendation made by a standard society (e.g. ACC/AHA) or consensus statement that denotes how to diagnose and treat a particular condition. Note: this type should be used to tag the actual guideline recommendation; if the guideline recommendation occurs in a larger scholarly article, use MedicalScholarlyArticle to tag the overall article, not this type. Note also: the organization making the recommendation should be captured in the recognizingAuthority base property of MedicalEntity.

nodes.label: MedicalGuidelineContraindication
nodes.description: A guideline contraindication that designates a process as harmful and where quality of the data supporting the contraindication is sound.

nodes.label: MedicalGuidelineRecommendation
nodes.description: A guideline recommendation that is regarded as efficacious and where quality of the data supporting the recommendation is sound.

nodes.label: MedicalImagingTechnique
nodes.description: Any medical imaging modality typically used for diagnostic purposes. Enumerated type.

nodes.label: MedicalIndication
nodes.description: A condition or factor that indicates use of a medical therapy, including signs, symptoms, risk factors, anatomical states, etc.

nodes.label: MedicalIntangible
nodes.description: A utility class that serves as the umbrella for a number of 'intangible' things in the medical space.

nodes.label: MedicalObservationalStudy
nodes.description: An observational study is a type of medical study that attempts to infer the possible effect of a treatment through observation of a cohort of subjects over a period of time. In an observational study, the assignment of subjects into treatment groups versus control groups is outside the control of the investigator. This is in contrast with controlled studies, such as the randomized controlled trials represented by MedicalTrial, where each subject is randomly assigned to a treatment group or a control group before the start of the treatment.

nodes.label: MedicalObservationalStudyDesign
nodes.description: Design models for observational medical studies. Enumerated type.

nodes.label: MedicalOrganization
nodes.description: A medical organization (physical or not), such as hospital, institution or clinic.

nodes.label: MedicalProcedure
nodes.description: A process of care used in either a diagnostic, therapeutic, preventive or palliative capacity that relies on invasive (surgical), non-invasive, or other techniques.

nodes.label: MedicalProcedureType
nodes.description: An enumeration that describes different types of medical procedures.

nodes.label: MedicalResearcher
nodes.description: Medical researchers.

nodes.label: MedicalRiskCalculator
nodes.description: A complex mathematical calculation requiring an online calculator, used to assess prognosis. Note: use the url property of Thing to record any URLs for online calculators.

nodes.label: MedicalRiskEstimator
nodes.description: Any rule set or interactive tool for estimating the risk of developing a complication or condition.

nodes.label: MedicalRiskFactor
nodes.description: A risk factor is anything that increases a person's likelihood of developing or contracting a disease, medical condition, or complication.

nodes.label: MedicalRiskScore
nodes.description: A simple system that adds up the number of risk factors to yield a score that is associated with prognosis, e.g. CHAD score, TIMI risk score.

nodes.label: MedicalScholarlyArticle
nodes.description: A scholarly article in the medical domain.

nodes.label: MedicalSign
nodes.description: Any physical manifestation of a person's medical condition discoverable by objective diagnostic tests or physical examination.

nodes.label: MedicalSignOrSymptom
nodes.description: Any feature associated or not with a medical condition. In medicine a symptom is generally subjective while a sign is objective.

nodes.label: MedicalSpecialty
nodes.description: Any specific branch of medical science or practice. Medical specialities include clinical specialties that pertain to particular organ systems and their respective disease states, as well as allied health specialties. Enumerated type.

nodes.label: MedicalStudy
nodes.description: A medical study is an umbrella type covering all kinds of research studies relating to human medicine or health, including observational studies and interventional trials and registries, randomized, controlled or not. When the specific type of study is known, use one of the extensions of this type, such as MedicalTrial or MedicalObservationalStudy. Also, note that this type should be used to mark up data that describes the study itself; to tag an article that publishes the results of a study, use MedicalScholarlyArticle. Note: use the code property of MedicalEntity to store study IDs, e.g. clinicaltrials.gov ID.

nodes.label: MedicalStudyStatus
nodes.description: The status of a medical study. Enumerated type.

nodes.label: MedicalSymptom
nodes.description: Any complaint sensed and expressed by the patient (therefore defined as subjective)  like stomachache, lower-back pain, or fatigue.

nodes.label: MedicalTest
nodes.description: Any medical test, typically performed for diagnostic purposes.

nodes.label: MedicalTestPanel
nodes.description: Any collection of tests commonly ordered together.

nodes.label: MedicalTherapy
nodes.description: Any medical intervention designed to prevent, treat, and cure human diseases and medical conditions, including both curative and palliative therapies. Medical therapies are typically processes of care relying upon pharmacotherapy, behavioral therapy, supportive therapy (with fluid or nutrition for example), or detoxification (e.g. hemodialysis) aimed at improving or preventing a health condition.

nodes.label: MedicalTrial
nodes.description: A medical trial is a type of medical study that uses a scientific process to compare the safety and efficacy of medical therapies or medical procedures. In general, medical trials are controlled and subjects are allocated at random to the different treatment and/or control groups.

nodes.label: MedicalTrialDesign
nodes.description: Design models for medical trials. Enumerated type.

nodes.label: MedicalWebPage
nodes.description: A web page that provides medical information.

nodes.label: MedicineSystem
nodes.description: Systems of medical practice.

nodes.label: MeetingRoom
nodes.description:
A meeting room, conference room, or conference hall is a room provided for singular events such as business conferences and meetings (source: Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia, see http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conference_hall).

See also the dedicated document on the use of schema.org for marking up hotels and other forms of accommodations.

nodes.label: MemberProgram
nodes.description: A MemberProgram defines a loyalty (or membership) program that provides its members with certain benefits, for example better pricing, free shipping or returns, or the ability to earn loyalty points. Member programs may have multiple tiers, for example silver and gold members, each with different benefits.

nodes.label: MemberProgramTier
nodes.description: A MemberProgramTier specifies a tier under a loyalty (member) program, for example "gold".

nodes.label: MensClothingStore
nodes.description: A men's clothing store.

nodes.label: Menu
nodes.description: A structured representation of food or drink items available from a FoodEstablishment.

nodes.label: MenuItem
nodes.description: A food or drink item listed in a menu or menu section.

nodes.label: MenuSection
nodes.description: A sub-grouping of food or drink items in a menu. E.g. courses (such as 'Dinner', 'Breakfast', etc.), specific type of dishes (such as 'Meat', 'Vegan', 'Drinks', etc.), or some other classification made by the menu provider.

nodes.label: MerchantReturnEnumeration
nodes.description: Enumerates several kinds of product return policies.

nodes.label: MerchantReturnFiniteReturnWindow
nodes.description: Specifies that there is a finite window for product returns.

nodes.label: MerchantReturnNotPermitted
nodes.description: Specifies that product returns are not permitted.

nodes.label: MerchantReturnPolicy
nodes.description: A MerchantReturnPolicy provides information about product return policies associated with an [[Organization]], [[Product]], or [[Offer]].

nodes.label: MerchantReturnPolicySeasonalOverride
nodes.description: A seasonal override of a return policy, for example used for holidays.

nodes.label: MerchantReturnUnlimitedWindow
nodes.description: Specifies that there is an unlimited window for product returns.

nodes.label: MerchantReturnUnspecified
nodes.description: Specifies that a product return policy is not provided.

nodes.label: Message
nodes.description: A single message from a sender to one or more organizations or people.

nodes.label: MiddleSchool
nodes.description: A middle school (typically for children aged around 11-14, although this varies somewhat).

nodes.label: Midwifery
nodes.description: A nurse-like health profession that deals with pregnancy, childbirth, and the postpartum period (including care of the newborn), besides sexual and reproductive health of women throughout their lives.

nodes.label: MinimumAdvertisedPrice

nodes.label: MinorHumanEditsDigitalSource
nodes.description: Content coded as 'minor human edits' using the IPTC digital source type vocabulary.

nodes.label: MisconceptionsHealthAspect
nodes.description: Content about common misconceptions and myths that are related to a topic.

nodes.label: MixedEventAttendanceMode

nodes.label: MixtapeAlbum
nodes.description: MixtapeAlbum.

nodes.label: MobileApplication
nodes.description: A software application designed specifically to work well on a mobile device such as a telephone.

nodes.label: MobilePhoneStore
nodes.description: A store that sells mobile phones and related accessories.

nodes.label: MobileWebPlatform
nodes.description: Represents the broad notion of 'mobile' browsers as a Web Platform.

nodes.label: MolecularEntity
nodes.description: Any constitutionally or isotopically distinct atom, molecule, ion, ion pair, radical, radical ion, complex, conformer etc., identifiable as a separately distinguishable entity.

nodes.label: Monday

nodes.label: MonetaryAmount
nodes.description: A monetary value or range. This type can be used to describe an amount of money such as $50 USD, or a range as in describing a bank account being suitable for a balance between £1,000 and £1,000,000 GBP, or the value of a salary, etc. It is recommended to use [[PriceSpecification]] Types to describe the price of an Offer, Invoice, etc.

nodes.label: MonetaryAmountDistribution

nodes.label: MonetaryGrant

nodes.label: MoneyTransfer

nodes.label: Number

Data type: Number.

Usage guidelines:

* Use values from 0123456789 (Unicode 'DIGIT ZERO' (U+0030) to 'DIGIT NINE' (U+0039)) rather than superficially similar Unicode symbols.
* Use '.' (Unicode 'FULL STOP' (U+002E)) rather than ',' to indicate a decimal point. Avoid using these symbols as a readability separator.

nodes.label: Observation
nodes.description:
Instances of the class [[Observation]] are used to specify observations about an entity at a particular time. The principal properties of an [[Observation]] are [[observationAbout]], [[measuredProperty]], [[statType]], [[value] and [[observationDate]]  and [[measuredProperty]]. Some but not all Observations represent a [[QuantitativeValue]]. Quantitative observations can be about a [[StatisticalVariable]], which is an abstract specification about which we can make observations that are grounded at a particular location and time.

Observations can also encode a subset of simple RDF-like statements (its observationAbout, a StatisticalVariable, defining the measuredPoperty; its observationAbout property indicating the entity the statement is about, and [[value]] )

In the context of a quantitative knowledge graph, typical properties could include [[measuredProperty]], [[observationAbout]], [[observationDate]], [[value]], [[unitCode]], [[unitText]], [[measurementMethod]].

nodes.label: Observational
nodes.description: An observational study design.

nodes.label: Obstetric

nodes.label: Occupation

nodes.label: OceanBodyOfWater

nodes.label: Offer
nodes.description:
An offer to transfer some rights to an item or to provide a service — for example, an offer to sell tickets to an event, to rent the DVD of a movie, to stream a TV show over the internet, to repair a motorcycle, or to loan a book.

Note: As the [[businessFunction]] property, which identifies the form of offer (e.g. sell, lease, repair, dispose), defaults to http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Sell; an Offer without a defined businessFunction value can be assumed to be an offer to sell.

For [GTIN](http://www.gs1.org/barcodes/technical/idkeys/gtin)-related fields, see [Check Digit calculator](http://www.gs1.org/barcodes/support/check_digit_calculator) and [validation guide](http://www.gs1us.org/resources/standards/gtin-validation-guide) from [GS1](http://www.gs1.org/).

nodes.label: OfferCatalog

nodes.label: OfferForLease

An [[OfferForLease]] in Schema.org represents an [[Offer]] to lease out something, i.e. an [[Offer]] whose
  [[businessFunction]] is [lease out](http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#LeaseOut.). See [Good Relations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GoodRelations) for
  background on the underlying concepts.

nodes.label: OfferForPurchase
nodes.description:
An [[OfferForPurchase]] in Schema.org represents an [[Offer]] to sell something, i.e. an [[Offer]] whose
  [[businessFunction]] is [sell](http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Sell.). See [Good Relations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GoodRelations) for
  background on the underlying concepts.

nodes.label: OfferShippingDetails
nodes.description:
OfferShippingDetails represents information about shipping destinations.

Multiple of these entities can be used to represent different shipping rates for different destinations:

One entity for Alaska/Hawaii. A different one for continental US. A different one for all France.

Multiple of these entities can be used to represent different shipping costs and delivery times.

Two entities that are identical but differ in rate and time:

E.g. Cheaper and slower: $5 in 5-7 days
or Fast and expensive: $15 in 1-2 days.
