nodes.description: OrderStatus representing successful delivery of an order.

nodes.label: OrderInTransit
nodes.description: OrderStatus representing that an order is in transit.

nodes.label: OrderItem
nodes.description: An order item is a line of an order. It includes the quantity and shipping details of a bought offer.

nodes.label: OrderPaymentDue
nodes.description: OrderStatus representing that payment is due on an order.

nodes.label: OrderPickupAvailable
nodes.description: OrderStatus representing availability of an order for pickup.

nodes.label: OrderProblem
nodes.description: OrderStatus representing that there is a problem with the order.

nodes.label: OrderProcessing
nodes.description: OrderStatus representing that an order is being processed.

nodes.label: OrderReturned
nodes.description: OrderStatus representing that an order has been returned.

nodes.label: OrderStatus
nodes.description: Enumerated status values for Order.

nodes.label: Organization
nodes.description: An organization such as a school, NGO, corporation, club, etc.

nodes.label: OrganizationRole
nodes.description: A subclass of Role used to describe roles within organizations.

nodes.label: OrganizeAction
nodes.description: The act of manipulating/administering/supervising/controlling one or more objects.

nodes.label: OriginalMediaContent
nodes.description:
Content coded 'as original media content' in a [[MediaReview]], considered in the context of how it was published or shared.

For a [[VideoObject]] to be 'original': No evidence the footage has been misleadingly altered or manipulated, though it may contain false or misleading claims.

For an [[ImageObject]] to be 'original': No evidence the image has been misleadingly altered or manipulated, though it may still contain false or misleading claims.

For an [[ImageObject]] with embedded text to be 'original': No evidence the image has been misleadingly altered or manipulated, though it may still contain false or misleading claims.

For an [[AudioObject]] to be 'original': No evidence the audio has been misleadingly altered or manipulated, though it may contain false or misleading claims.

nodes.label: OriginalShippingFees
nodes.description: Specifies that the customer must pay the original shipping costs when returning a product.

nodes.label: Osteopathic
nodes.description: A system of medicine focused on promoting the body's innate ability to heal itself.

nodes.label: Otolaryngologic
nodes.description: A specific branch of medical science that is concerned with the ear, nose and throat and their respective disease states.

nodes.label: OutOfStock
nodes.description: Indicates that the item is out of stock.

nodes.label: OutletStore
nodes.description: An outlet store.

nodes.label: OverviewHealthAspect
nodes.description: Overview of the content. Contains a summarized view of the topic with the most relevant information for an introduction.

nodes.label: OwnershipInfo
nodes.description: A structured value providing information about when a certain organization or person owned a certain product.

nodes.label: PET
nodes.description: Positron emission tomography imaging.

nodes.label: PaidLeave
nodes.description: PaidLeave: this is a benefit for paid leave.

nodes.label: PaintAction
nodes.description: The act of producing a painting, typically with paint and canvas as instruments.

nodes.label: Painting
nodes.description: A painting.

nodes.label: PalliativeProcedure
nodes.description: A medical procedure intended primarily for palliative purposes, aimed at relieving the symptoms of an underlying health condition.

nodes.label: Pamphlet
nodes.description: A small, unbound or stapled booklet consisting of few pages with a flexible paper cover, designed for the economical distribution of focused information on a single subject.

nodes.label: Paperback
nodes.description: A flexible, lightweight book bound with a thick paper or cardstock cover and glued spine, prioritizing portability and affordability over long-term durability.

nodes.label: ParcelDelivery
nodes.description: The delivery of a parcel either via the postal service or a commercial service.

nodes.label: ParcelService
nodes.description:
A private parcel service as the delivery mode available for a certain offer.

Commonly used values:

* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#DHL
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#FederalExpress
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#UPS

nodes.label: ParentAudience
nodes.description: A set of characteristics describing parents, who can be interested in viewing some content.

nodes.label: ParentalSupport
nodes.description: ParentalSupport: this is a benefit for parental support.

nodes.label: Park
nodes.description: A park.

nodes.label: ParkingFacility
nodes.description: A parking lot or other parking facility.

nodes.label: ParkingMap
nodes.description: A parking map.

nodes.label: PartiallyInForce
nodes.description: Indicates that parts of the legislation are in force, and parts are not.

nodes.label: Pathology
nodes.description: A specific branch of medical science that is concerned with the study of the cause, origin and nature of a disease state, including its consequences as a result of manifestation of the disease. In clinical care, the term is used to designate a branch of medicine using laboratory tests to diagnose and determine the prognostic significance of illness.

nodes.label: PathologyTest
nodes.description: A medical test performed by a laboratory that typically involves examination of a tissue sample by a pathologist.

nodes.label: Patient
nodes.description: A patient is any person recipient of health care services.

nodes.label: PatientExperienceHealthAspect
nodes.description: Content about the real life experience of patients or people that have lived a similar experience about the topic. May be forums, topics, Q-and-A and related material.

nodes.label: PawnShop
nodes.description: A shop that will buy, or lend money against the security of, personal possessions.

nodes.label: PayAction
nodes.description: An agent pays a price to a participant.

nodes.label: PaymentAutomaticallyApplied
nodes.description: An automatic payment system is in place and will be used.

nodes.label: PaymentCard
nodes.description: A payment method using a credit, debit, store or other card to associate the payment with an account.

nodes.label: PaymentChargeSpecification
nodes.description: The costs of settling the payment using a particular payment method.

nodes.label: PaymentComplete
nodes.description: The payment has been received and processed.

nodes.label: PaymentDeclined
nodes.description: The payee received the payment, but it was declined for some reason.

nodes.label: PaymentDue
nodes.description: The payment is due, but still within an acceptable time to be received.

nodes.label: PaymentMethod
nodes.description:
A payment method is a standardized procedure for transferring the monetary amount for a purchase. Payment methods are characterized by the legal and technical structures used, and by the organization or group carrying out the transaction. The following legacy values should be accepted: 

* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#ByBankTransferInAdvance
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#ByInvoice
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#Cash
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#CheckInAdvance
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#COD
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#DirectDebit
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#GoogleCheckout
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#PayPal
* http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#PaySwarm

Structured values, or [UNCE payment means](https://vocabulary.uncefact.org/PaymentMeans) are recommended or for newer annotations.

nodes.label: PaymentMethodType
nodes.description: The type of payment method, only for generic payment types, specific forms of payments, like card payment should be expressed using subclasses of PaymentMethod.

nodes.label: PaymentPastDue
nodes.description: The payment is due and considered late.

nodes.label: PaymentService
nodes.description: A Service to transfer funds from a person or organization to a beneficiary person or organization.

nodes.label: PaymentStatusType
nodes.description: A specific payment status. For example, PaymentDue, PaymentComplete, etc.

nodes.label: Pediatric
nodes.description: A specific branch of medical science that specializes in the care of infants, children and adolescents.

nodes.label: PeopleAudience
nodes.description: A set of characteristics belonging to people, e.g. who compose an item's target audience.

nodes.label: PercutaneousProcedure
nodes.description: A type of medical procedure that involves percutaneous techniques, where access to organs or tissue is achieved via needle-puncture of the skin. For example, catheter-based procedures like stent delivery.

nodes.label: PerformAction
nodes.description: The act of participating in performance arts.

nodes.label: PerformanceRole
nodes.description: A PerformanceRole is a Role that some entity places with regard to a theatrical performance, e.g. in a Movie, TVSeries etc.

nodes.label: PerformingArtsEvent
nodes.description:
Live performance Event of the performing arts (music, theatre, dance, acrobatics, spoken word), including performance art and performative sports (e.g. choreographed forms of martial arts, figure skating, competitive ballroom dancing).

Note: Use additionalType to differentiate between productions / shows (PerformanceWork, EventSeries), tours (EventSeries), and individual performances.

nodes.label: PerformingArtsTheater
nodes.description: A theater or other performing art center.

nodes.label: PerformingGroup
nodes.description: A performance group, such as a band, an orchestra, or a circus.

nodes.label: Periodical
nodes.description: A publication in any medium issued in successive parts bearing numerical or chronological designations and intended to continue indefinitely, such as a magazine, scholarly journal, or newspaper.\n\nSee also [blog post](https://blog.schema.org/2014/09/02/schema-org-support-for-bibliographic-relationships-and-periodicals/).

nodes.label: Permit
nodes.description: A permit issued by an organization, e.g. a parking pass.

nodes.label: Person
nodes.description: A person (alive, dead, undead, or fictional).

nodes.label: PetStore
nodes.description: A pet store.

nodes.label: Pharmacy
nodes.description: A pharmacy or drugstore.

nodes.label: PharmacySpecialty
nodes.description: The practice or art and science of preparing and dispensing drugs and medicines.

nodes.label: PhoneCarrierPayment
nodes.description: Payment by billing via the phone carrier.

nodes.label: Photograph
nodes.description: A photograph.

nodes.label: PhotographAction
nodes.description: The act of capturing still images of objects using a camera.

nodes.label: PhysicalActivity
nodes.description: Any bodily activity that enhances or maintains physical fitness and overall health and wellness. Includes activity that is part of daily living and routine, structured exercise, and exercise prescribed as part of a medical treatment or recovery plan.

nodes.label: PhysicalActivityCategory
nodes.description: Categories of physical activity, organized by physiologic classification.

nodes.label: PhysicalExam
nodes.description: A type of physical examination of a patient performed by a physician.

nodes.label: PhysicalTherapy
nodes.description: A process of progressive physical care and rehabilitation aimed at improving a health condition.

nodes.label: Physician
nodes.description: An individual physician or a physician's office considered as a [[MedicalOrganization]].

nodes.label: PhysiciansOffice
nodes.description: A doctor's office or clinic.

nodes.label: Physiotherapy
nodes.description: The practice of treatment of disease, injury, or deformity by physical methods such as massage, heat treatment, and exercise rather than by drugs or surgery.

nodes.label: Place
nodes.description: Entities that have a somewhat fixed, physical extension.

nodes.label: PlaceOfWorship
nodes.description: Place of worship, such as a church, synagogue, or mosque.

nodes.label: PlaceboControlledTrial
nodes.description: A placebo-controlled trial design.

nodes.label: PlanAction
nodes.description: The act of planning the execution of an event/task/action/reservation/plan to a future date.

nodes.label: PlasticSurgery
nodes.description: A specific branch of medical science that pertains to therapeutic or cosmetic repair or re-formation of missing, injured or malformed tissues or body parts by manual and instrumental means.

nodes.label: Play
nodes.description: A play is a form of literature, usually consisting of dialogue between characters, intended for theatrical performance rather than just reading. Note: A performance of a Play would be a [[TheaterEvent]] or [[BroadcastEvent]] - the *Play* being the [[workPerformed]].

nodes.label: PlayAction
nodes.description:
The act of playing/exercising/training/performing for enjoyment, leisure, recreation, competition or exercise.

Related actions:

* [[ListenAction]]: Unlike ListenAction (which is under ConsumeAction), PlayAction refers to performing for an audience or at an event, rather than consuming music.
* [[WatchAction]]: Unlike WatchAction (which is under ConsumeAction), PlayAction refers to showing/displaying for an audience or at an event, rather than consuming visual content.

nodes.label: PlayGameAction
nodes.description: The act of playing a video game.

nodes.label: Playground
nodes.description: A playground.

nodes.label: Plumber
nodes.description: A plumbing service.

nodes.label: PodcastEpisode
nodes.description: A single episode of a podcast series.

nodes.label: PodcastSeason
nodes.description: A single season of a podcast. Many podcasts do not break down into separate seasons. In that case, PodcastSeries should be used.

nodes.label: PodcastSeries
nodes.description: A podcast is an episodic series of digital audio or video files which a user can download and listen to.

nodes.label: Podiatric
nodes.description: Podiatry is the care of the human foot, especially the diagnosis and treatment of foot disorders.

nodes.label: PoliceStation
nodes.description: A police station.

nodes.label: PoliticalParty
nodes.description: Organization: Political Party.

nodes.label: Pond
nodes.description: A pond.

nodes.label: PositiveFilmDigitalSource
nodes.description: Content coded as 'positive film' using the IPTC digital source type vocabulary.

nodes.label: PostOffice
nodes.description: A post office.

nodes.label: PostalAddress
nodes.description: The mailing address.

nodes.label: PostalCodeRangeSpecification
nodes.description: Indicates a range of postal codes, usually defined as the set of valid codes between [[postalCodeBegin]] and [[postalCodeEnd]], inclusively.

nodes.label: Poster
nodes.description: A large, usually printed placard, bill, or announcement, often illustrated, that is posted to advertise or publicize something.

nodes.label: PotentialActionStatus
nodes.description: A description of an action that is supported.

nodes.label: PreOrder
nodes.description: Indicates that the item is available for pre-order.

nodes.label: PreOrderAction
nodes.description: An agent orders a (not yet released) object/product/service to be delivered/sent.

nodes.label: PreSale
nodes.description: Indicates that the item is available for ordering and delivery before general availability.

nodes.label: PregnancyHealthAspect
nodes.description: Content discussing pregnancy-related aspects of a health topic.

nodes.label: PrependAction
nodes.description: The act of inserting at the beginning if an ordered collection.

nodes.label: Preschool
nodes.description: A preschool.

nodes.label: PrescriptionOnly
nodes.description: Available by prescription only.

nodes.label: PresentationDigitalDocument
nodes.description: A file containing slides or used for a presentation.

nodes.label: PreventionHealthAspect
nodes.description: Information about actions or measures that can be taken to avoid getting the topic or reaching a critical situation related to the topic.

nodes.label: PreventionIndication
nodes.description: An indication for preventing an underlying condition, symptom, etc.

nodes.label: PriceComponentTypeEnumeration
nodes.description: Enumerates different price components that together make up the total price for an offered product.

nodes.label: PriceSpecification
nodes.description: A structured value representing a price or price range. Typically, only the subclasses of this type are used for markup. It is recommended to use [[MonetaryAmount]] to describe independent amounts of money such as a salary, credit card limits, etc.

nodes.label: PriceTypeEnumeration
nodes.description: Enumerates different price types, for example list price, invoice price, and sale price.

nodes.label: PrimaryCare
nodes.description: The medical care by a physician, or other health-care professional, who is the patient's first contact with the health-care system and who may recommend a specialist if necessary.

nodes.label: PrintDigitalSource
nodes.description: Content coded as 'print' using the IPTC digital source type vocabulary.

nodes.label: Prion
nodes.description: A prion is an infectious agent composed of protein in a misfolded form.

nodes.label: Product
nodes.description: Any offered product or service. For example: a pair of shoes; a concert ticket; the rental of a car; a haircut; or an episode of a TV show streamed online.

nodes.label: ProductCollection
nodes.description: A set of products (either [[ProductGroup]]s or specific variants) that are listed together e.g. in an [[Offer]].

nodes.label: ProductGroup
nodes.description:
A ProductGroup represents a group of [[Product]]s that vary only in certain well-described ways, such as by [[size]], [[color]], [[material]] etc.

While a ProductGroup itself is not directly offered for sale, the various varying products that it represents can be. The ProductGroup serves as a prototype or template, standing in for all of the products who have an [[isVariantOf]] relationship to it. As such, properties (including additional types) can be applied to the ProductGroup to represent characteristics shared by each of the (possibly very many) variants. Properties that reference a ProductGroup are not included in this mechanism; neither are the following specific properties [[variesBy]], [[hasVariant]], [[url]].

nodes.label: ProductModel
nodes.description: A datasheet or vendor specification of a product (in the sense of a prototypical description).

nodes.label: ProductReturnEnumeration
nodes.description: ProductReturnEnumeration enumerates several kinds of product return policy. Note that this structure may not capture all aspects of the policy.

nodes.label: ProductReturnFiniteReturnWindow
nodes.description: ProductReturnFiniteReturnWindow: there is a finite window for product returns.

nodes.label: ProductReturnNotPermitted
nodes.description: ProductReturnNotPermitted: product returns are not permitted.

nodes.label: ProductReturnPolicy
nodes.description: A ProductReturnPolicy provides information about product return policies associated with an [[Organization]] or [[Product]].

nodes.label: ProductReturnUnlimitedWindow
nodes.description: ProductReturnUnlimitedWindow: there is an unlimited window for product returns.

nodes.label: ProductReturnUnspecified
nodes.description: ProductReturnUnspecified: a product return policy is not specified here.

nodes.label: ProfessionalService
nodes.description:
Original definition: "provider of professional services."\n\nThe general [[ProfessionalService]] type for local businesses was deprecated due to confusion with [[Service]]. For reference, the types that it included were: [[Dentist]],
        [[AccountingService]], [[Attorney]], [[Notary]], as well as types for several kinds of [[HomeAndConstructionBusiness]]: [[Electrician]], [[GeneralContractor]],
        [[HousePainter]], [[Locksmith]], [[Plumber]], [[RoofingContractor]]. [[LegalService]] was introduced as a more inclusive supertype of [[Attorney]].

nodes.label: ProfilePage
nodes.description: Web page type: Profile page.

nodes.label: PrognosisHealthAspect
nodes.description: Typical progression and happenings of life course of the topic.

nodes.label: ProgramMembership
nodes.description: Used to describe membership in a loyalty programs (e.g. "StarAliance"), traveler clubs (e.g. "AAA"), purchase clubs ("Safeway Club"), etc.

nodes.label: Project
nodes.description:
An enterprise (potentially individual but typically collaborative), planned to achieve a particular aim.
Use properties from [[Organization]], [[subOrganization]]/[[parentOrganization]] to indicate project sub-structures.

nodes.label: PronounceableText
nodes.description: Data type: PronounceableText.

nodes.label: Property
nodes.description: A property, used to indicate attributes and relationships of some Thing; equivalent to rdf:Property.

nodes.label: PropertyValue
nodes.description: A property-value pair, e.g. representing a feature of a product or place. Use the 'name' property for the name of the property. If there is an additional human-readable version of the value, put that into the 'description' property.\n\n Always use specific schema.org properties when a) they exist and b) you can populate them. Using PropertyValue as a substitute will typically not trigger the same effect as using the original, specific property.

nodes.label: PropertyValueSpecification
nodes.description: A Property value specification.

nodes.label: Protein
nodes.description: Protein is here used in its widest possible definition, as classes of amino acid based molecules. Amyloid-beta Protein in human (UniProt P05067), eukaryota (e.g. an OrthoDB group) or even a single molecule that one can point to are all of type :Protein. A protein can thus be a subclass of another protein, e.g. :Protein as a UniProt record can have multiple isoforms inside it which would also be :Protein. They can be imagined, synthetic, hypothetical or naturally occurring.

nodes.label: Protozoa
nodes.description: Single-celled organism that causes an infection.

nodes.label: Psychiatric
nodes.description: A specific branch of medical science that is concerned with the study, treatment, and prevention of mental illness, using both medical and psychological therapies.

nodes.label: PsychologicalTreatment
nodes.description: A process of care relying upon counseling, dialogue and communication  aimed at improving a mental health condition without use of drugs.

nodes.label: PublicHealth
nodes.description: Branch of medicine that pertains to the health services to improve and protect community health, especially epidemiology, sanitation, immunization, and preventive medicine.

nodes.label: PublicHolidays
nodes.description: This stands for any day that is a public holiday; it is a placeholder for all official public holidays in some particular location. While not technically a "day of the week", it can be used with [[OpeningHoursSpecification]]. In the context of an opening hours specification it can be used to indicate opening hours on public holidays, overriding general opening hours for the day of the week on which a public holiday occurs.

nodes.label: PublicSwimmingPool
nodes.description: A public swimming pool.

nodes.label: PublicToilet
nodes.description: A public toilet is a room or small building containing one or more toilets (and possibly also urinals) which is available for use by the general public, or by customers or employees of certain businesses.

nodes.label: PublicationEvent
nodes.description: A PublicationEvent corresponds indifferently to the event of publication for a CreativeWork of any type, e.g. a broadcast event, an on-demand event, a book/journal publication via a variety of delivery media.

nodes.label: PublicationIssue
nodes.description: A part of a successively published publication such as a periodical or publication volume, often numbered, usually containing a grouping of works such as articles.\n\nSee also [blog post](https://blog-schema.org/2014/09/02/schema-org-support-for-bibliographic-relationships-and-periodicals/).

nodes.label: PublicationVolume
nodes.description: A part of a successively published publication such as a periodical or multi-volume work, often numbered. It may represent a time span, such as a year.\n\nSee also [blog post](https://blog-schema.org/2014/09/02/schema-org-support-for-bibliographic-relationships-and-periodicals/).

nodes.label: Pulmonary
nodes.description: A specific branch of medical science that pertains to the study of the respiratory system and its respective disease states.

nodes.label: PurchaseType
nodes.description: Enumerates a purchase type for an item.

nodes.label: PurchaseTypeLease
nodes.description: This is a lease of an item.

nodes.label: PurchaseTypeNewPurchase
nodes.description: This is a purchase of a new item.

nodes.label: PurchaseTypeTradeIn
nodes.description: This is a trade-in for an item.

nodes.label: PurchaseTypeUsedPurchase
nodes.description: This is a purchase of a used item.

nodes.label: QAPage
nodes.description: A QAPage is a WebPage focussed on a specific Question and its Answer(s), e.g. in a question answering site or documenting Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs).

nodes.label: QualitativeValue
nodes.description: A predefined value for a product characteristic, e.g. the power cord plug type 'US' or the garment sizes 'S', 'M', 'L', and 'XL'.

nodes.label: QuantitativeValue
nodes.description: A point value or interval for product characteristics and other purposes.

nodes.label: QuantitativeValueDistribution
nodes.description: A statistical distribution of values.

nodes.label: Quantity
nodes.description: Quantities such as distance, time, mass, weight, etc. Particular instances of say Mass are strings like '3 kg' or '4 milligrams'.

nodes.label: Question
nodes.description: A specific question - e.g. from a user seeking answers online, or collected in a Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) document.

nodes.label: Quiz
nodes.description: Quiz: A test of knowledge, skills and abilities.

nodes.label: Quotation
nodes.description: A quotation. Often but not necessarily from some written work, attributable to a real world author and - if associated with a fictional character - to any fictional Person. Use [[isBasedOn]] to link to source/origin. The [[recordedIn]] property can be used to reference a Quotation from an [[Event]].

nodes.label: QuoteAction
nodes.description: An agent quotes/estimates/appraises an object/product/service with a price at a location/store.

nodes.label: RVPark
nodes.description: A place offering space for "Recreational Vehicles", Caravans, mobile homes and the like.

nodes.label: RadiationTherapy
nodes.description: A process of care using radiation aimed at improving a health condition.

nodes.label: RadioBroadcastService
nodes.description: A delivery service through which radio content is provided via broadcast over the air or online.

nodes.label: RadioChannel
nodes.description: A unique instance of a radio BroadcastService on a CableOrSatelliteService lineup.

nodes.label: RadioClip
nodes.description: A short radio program or a segment/part of a radio program.

nodes.label: RadioEpisode
nodes.description: A radio episode which can be part of a series or season.

nodes.label: RadioSeason
nodes.description: Season dedicated to radio broadcast and associated online delivery.

nodes.label: RadioSeries
nodes.description: CreativeWorkSeries dedicated to radio broadcast and associated online delivery.

nodes.label: RadioStation
nodes.description: A radio station.

nodes.label: Radiography
nodes.description: Radiography is an imaging technique that uses electromagnetic radiation other than visible light, especially X-rays, to view the internal structure of a non-uniformly composed and opaque object such as the human body.

nodes.label: RandomizedTrial
nodes.description: A randomized trial design.

nodes.label: Rating
nodes.description: A rating is an evaluation on a numeric scale, such as 1 to 5 stars.

nodes.label: ReactAction
nodes.description: The act of responding instinctively and emotionally to an object, expressing a sentiment.

nodes.label: ReadAction
nodes.description: The act of consuming written content.

nodes.label: ReadPermission
nodes.description: Permission to read or view the document.

nodes.label: RealEstateAgent
nodes.description: A real-estate agent.

nodes.label: RealEstateListing
nodes.description:
A [[RealEstateListing]] is a listing that describes one or more real-estate [[Offer]]s (whose [[businessFunction]] is typically to lease out, or to sell).
  The [[RealEstateListing]] type itself represents the overall listing, as manifested in some [[WebPage]].

nodes.label: RearWheelDriveConfiguration
nodes.description: Real-wheel drive is a transmission layout where the engine drives the rear wheels.

nodes.label: ReceiveAction
nodes.description:
The act of physically/electronically taking delivery of an object that has been transferred from an origin to a destination. Reciprocal of SendAction.

Related actions:

* [[SendAction]]: The reciprocal of ReceiveAction.
* [[TakeAction]]: Unlike TakeAction, ReceiveAction does not imply that the ownership has been transferred (e.g. I can receive a package, but it does not mean the package is now mine).

nodes.label: Recipe
nodes.description: A recipe. For dietary restrictions covered by the recipe, a few common restrictions are enumerated via [[suitableForDiet]]. The [[keywords]] property can also be used to add more detail.

nodes.label: Recommendation
nodes.description: [[Recommendation]] is a type of [[Review]] that suggests or proposes something as the best option or best course of action. Recommendations may be for products or services, or other concrete things, as in the case of a ranked list or product guide. A [[Guide]] may list multiple recommendations for different categories. For example, in a [[Guide]] about which TVs to buy, the author may have several [[Recommendation]]s.

nodes.label: RecommendedDoseSchedule
nodes.description: A recommended dosing schedule for a drug or supplement as prescribed or recommended by an authority or by the drug/supplement's manufacturer. Capture the recommending authority in the recognizingAuthority property of MedicalEntity.

nodes.label: Recruiting
nodes.description: Recruiting participants.

nodes.label: RecyclingCenter
nodes.description: A recycling center.

nodes.label: ReducedRelevanceForChildrenConsideration
nodes.description: A general code for cases where relevance to children is reduced, e.g. adult education, mortgages, retirement-related products, etc.

nodes.label: RefundTypeEnumeration
nodes.description: Enumerates several kinds of product return refund types.

nodes.label: RefurbishedCondition
nodes.description: Indicates that the item is refurbished.

nodes.label: RegisterAction
nodes.description:
The act of registering to be a user of a service, product or web page.

Related actions:

* [[JoinAction]]: Unlike JoinAction, RegisterAction implies you are registering to be a user of a service, *not* a group/team of people.
* [[FollowAction]]: Unlike FollowAction, RegisterAction doesn't imply that the agent is expecting to poll for updates from the object.
* [[SubscribeAction]]: Unlike SubscribeAction, RegisterAction doesn't imply that the agent is expecting updates from the object.

nodes.label: Registry
nodes.description: A registry-based study design.

nodes.label: RegularPrice
nodes.description: Represents the regular price of an offered product. This is usually the advertised price before a temporary sale. Once the sale period ends the advertised price will go back to the regular price.

nodes.label: ReimbursementCap
nodes.description: The drug's cost represents the maximum reimbursement paid by an insurer for the drug.

nodes.label: RejectAction
nodes.description:
The act of rejecting to/adopting an object.

Related actions:

* [[AcceptAction]]: The antonym of RejectAction.

nodes.label: RelatedTopicsHealthAspect
nodes.description: Other prominent or relevant topics tied to the main topic.

nodes.label: RemixAlbum
nodes.description: RemixAlbum.

nodes.label: Renal
nodes.description: A specific branch of medical science that pertains to the study of the kidneys and its respective disease states.

nodes.label: RentAction
nodes.description: The act of giving money in return for temporary use, but not ownership, of an object such as a vehicle or property. For example, an agent rents a property from a landlord in exchange for a periodic payment.

nodes.label: RentalCarReservation
nodes.description: A reservation for a rental car.\n\nNote: This type is for information about actual reservations, e.g. in confirmation emails or HTML pages with individual confirmations of reservations.

nodes.label: RentalVehicleUsage
nodes.description: Indicates the usage of the vehicle as a rental car.

nodes.label: RepaymentSpecification
nodes.description: A structured value representing repayment.

nodes.label: ReplaceAction
nodes.description: The act of editing a recipient by replacing an old object with a new object.

nodes.label: ReplyAction
nodes.description:
The act of responding to a question/message asked/sent by the object. Related to [[AskAction]].

Related actions:

* [[AskAction]]: Appears generally as an origin of a ReplyAction.

nodes.label: Report
nodes.description: A Report generated by governmental or non-governmental organization.

nodes.label: ReportageNewsArticle
nodes.description:
The [[ReportageNewsArticle]] type is a subtype of [[NewsArticle]] representing
 news articles which are the result of journalistic news reporting conventions.

In practice many news publishers produce a wide variety of article types, many of which might be considered a [[NewsArticle]] but not a [[ReportageNewsArticle]]. For example, opinion pieces, reviews, analysis, sponsored or satirical articles, or articles that combine several of these elements.

The [[ReportageNewsArticle]] type is based on a stricter ideal for "news" as a work of journalism, with articles based on factual information either observed or verified by the author, or reported and verified from knowledgeable sources.  This often includes perspectives from multiple viewpoints on a particular issue (distinguishing news reports from public relations or propaganda).  News reports in the [[ReportageNewsArticle]] sense de-emphasize the opinion of the author, with commentary and value judgements typically expressed elsewhere.

A [[ReportageNewsArticle]] which goes deeper into analysis can also be marked with an additional type of [[AnalysisNewsArticle]].

nodes.label: ReportedDoseSchedule
nodes.description: A patient-reported or observed dosing schedule for a drug or supplement.

nodes.label: ResearchOrganization
nodes.description: A Research Organization (e.g. scientific institute, research company).

nodes.label: ResearchProject
nodes.description: A Research project.

nodes.label: Researcher
nodes.description: Researchers.

nodes.label: Reservation
nodes.description: Describes a reservation for travel, dining or an event. Some reservations require tickets. \n\nNote: This type is for information about actual reservations, e.g. in confirmation emails or HTML pages with individual confirmations of reservations. For offers of tickets, restaurant reservations, flights, or rental cars, use [[Offer]].

nodes.label: ReservationCancelled
nodes.description: The status for a previously confirmed reservation that is now cancelled.

nodes.label: ReservationConfirmed
nodes.description: The status of a confirmed reservation.

nodes.label: ReservationHold
nodes.description: The status of a reservation on hold pending an update like credit card number or flight changes.

nodes.label: ReservationPackage
nodes.description: A group of multiple reservations with common values for all sub-reservations.

nodes.label: ReservationPending
nodes.description: The status of a reservation when a request has been sent, but not confirmed.

nodes.label: ReservationStatusType

nodes.label: ReserveAction
nodes.description:
Reserving a concrete object.

Related actions:

* [[ScheduleAction]]: Unlike ScheduleAction, ReserveAction reserves concrete objects (e.g. a table, a hotel) towards a time slot / spatial allocation.

nodes.label: Reserved
nodes.description: Indicates that the item is reserved and therefore not available.

nodes.label: Reservoir
nodes.description: A reservoir of water, typically an artificially created lake, like the Lake Kariba reservoir.

nodes.label: ResetPasswordAction
nodes.description: The action of resetting the password of a device or application.

nodes.label: Residence
nodes.description: The place where a person lives.

nodes.label: Resort
nodes.description:
A resort is a place used for relaxation or recreation, attracting visitors for holidays or vacations. Resorts are places, towns or sometimes commercial establishments operated by a single company (source: Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia, see http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Resort).

See also the dedicated document on the use of schema.org for marking up hotels and other forms of accommodations.

nodes.label: RespiratoryTherapy
nodes.description: The therapy that is concerned with the maintenance or improvement of respiratory function (as in patients with pulmonary disease).

nodes.label: Restaurant

nodes.label: RestockingFees

nodes.label: RestrictedDiet

nodes.label: Retail

nodes.label: ReturnAction

nodes.label: ReturnLabelInBox

nodes.label: ReturnMethodEnumeration

nodes.label: ReturnShippingFees

nodes.label: Review

Such properties can be attached to a Role entity, which is then associated with the main entities using ordinary properties like 'member' or 'actor'.\n\nSee also [blog post](https://blog.schema.org/2014/06/16/introducing-role/).

nodes.label: SatireOrParodyContent
nodes.description:

For a [[VideoObject]] to be 'satire or parody content': A video that was created as political or humorous commentary and is presented in that context. (Reshares of satire/parody content that do not include relevant context are more likely to fall under the “missing context” rating.)

For an [[ImageObject]] to be 'satire or parody content': An image that was created as political or humorous commentary and is presented in that context. (Reshares of satire/parody content that do not include relevant context are more likely to fall under the “missing context” rating.)

For an [[ImageObject]] with embedded text to be 'satire or parody content': An image that was created as political or humorous commentary and is presented in that context. (Reshares of satire/parody content that do not include relevant context are more likely to fall under the “missing context” rating.)

For an [[AudioObject]] to be 'satire or parody content': Audio that was created as political or humorous commentary and is presented in that context. (Reshares of satire/parody content that do not include relevant context are more likely to fall under the “missing context” rating.)

nodes.label: SatiricalArticle

nodes.label: Schedule
nodes.description:
A schedule defines a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring [[Event]]. At a minimum a schedule will specify [[repeatFrequency]] which describes the interval between occurrences of the event. Additional information can be provided to specify the schedule more precisely.
      This includes identifying the day(s) of the week or month when the recurring event will take place, in addition to its start and end time. Schedules may also
      have start and end dates to indicate when they are active, e.g. to define a limited calendar of events.

nodes.label: ScheduleAction
nodes.description:
Scheduling future actions, events, or tasks.

Related actions:

* [[ReserveAction]]: Unlike ReserveAction, ScheduleAction allocates future actions (e.g. an event, a task, etc) towards a time slot / spatial allocation.

nodes.label: SendAction

The act of physically/electronically dispatching an object for transfer from an origin to a destination. Related actions:

* [[ReceiveAction]]: The reciprocal of SendAction.
* [[GiveAction]]: Unlike GiveAction, SendAction does not imply the transfer of ownership (e.g. I can send you my laptop, but I'm not necessarily giving it to you).

nodes.label: SequentialArt
nodes.description: An art forms that use images deployed in a specific order for the purpose of graphic storytelling (i.e., narration of graphic stories) or conveying information. Examples of SequentialArt are Franco-Belgian Bande Dessinée, Comics in the USA and 漫画 (Manga) in Japan.

nodes.label: Series

nodes.label: ServicePeriod

nodes.label: SexualContentConsideration

Such conditions may apply to only a subset of the products being shipped, depending on aspects of the product like weight, size, price, destination, and others. In addition, the intended audience can be defined through [[suggestedAge]], [[suggestedGender]], and suggested body measurements ([[suggestedMeasurement]]).

nodes.label: SpecialAnnouncement
nodes.description:
A SpecialAnnouncement combines a simple date-stamped textual information update
      with contextualized Web links and other structured data.  It represents an information update made by a
      locally-oriented organization, for example schools, pharmacies, healthcare providers,  community groups, police,
      local government.

For work in progress guidelines on Coronavirus-related markup see [this doc](https://docs.google.com/document/d/14ikaGCKxo50rRM7nvKSlbUpjyIk2WMQd3IkB1lItlrM/edit#).

The motivating scenario for SpecialAnnouncement is the [Coronavirus pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019%E2%80%9320_coronavirus_pandemic), and the initial vocabulary is oriented to this urgent situation. Schema.org
expect to improve the markup iteratively as it is deployed and as feedback emerges from use. In addition to our
usual [Github entry](https://github.com/schemaorg/schemaorg/issues/2490), feedback comments can also be provided in [this document](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1fpdFFxk8s87CWwACs53SGkYv3aafSxz_DTtOQxMrBJQ/edit#).


While this schema is designed to communicate urgent crisis-related information, it is not the same as an emergency warning technology like [CAP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Common_Alerting_Protocol), although there may be overlaps. The intent is to cover
the kinds of everyday practical information being posted to existing websites during an emergency situation.

Several kinds of information can be provided:

We encourage the provision of "name", "text", "datePosted", "expires" (if appropriate), "category" and
"url" as a simple baseline. It is important to provide a value for "category" where possible, most ideally as a well known
URL from Wikipedia or Wikidata. In the case of the 2019-2020 Coronavirus pandemic, this should be "https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2019-20\_coronavirus\_pandemic" or "https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q81068910".

For many of the possible properties, values can either be simple links or an inline description, depending on whether a summary is available. For a link, provide just the URL of the appropriate page as the property's value. For an inline description, use a [[WebContent]] type, and provide the url as a property of that, alongside at least a simple "[[text]]" summary of the page. It is
unlikely that a single SpecialAnnouncement will need all of the possible properties simultaneously.

We expect that in many cases the page referenced might contain more specialized structured data, e.g. contact info, [[openingHours]], [[Event]], [[FAQPage]] etc. By linking to those pages from a [[SpecialAnnouncement]] you can help make it clearer that the events are related to the situation (e.g. Coronavirus) indicated by the [[category]] property of the [[SpecialAnnouncement]].

Many [[SpecialAnnouncement]]s will relate to particular regions and to identifiable local organizations. Use [[spatialCoverage]] for the region, and [[announcementLocation]] to indicate specific [[LocalBusiness]]es and [[CivicStructure]]s. If the announcement affects both a particular region and a specific location (for example, a library closure that serves an entire region), use both [[spatialCoverage]] and [[announcementLocation]].

The [[about]] property can be used to indicate entities that are the focus of the announcement. We now recommend using [[about]] only
for representing non-location entities (e.g. a [[Course]] or a [[RadioStation]]). For places, use [[announcementLocation]] and [[spatialCoverage]]. Consumers of this markup should be aware that the initial design encouraged the use of [[about]] for locations too.

The basic content of [[SpecialAnnouncement]] is similar to that of an [RSS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RSS) or [Atom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atom_(Web_standard)) feed. For publishers without such feeds, basic feed-like information can be shared by posting
[[SpecialAnnouncement]] updates in a page, e.g. using JSON-LD. For sites with Atom/RSS functionality, you can point to a feed
with the [[webFeed]] property. This can be a simple URL, or an inline [[DataFeed]] object, with [[encodingFormat]] providing
media type information, e.g. "application/rss+xml" or "application/atom+xml".

nodes.label: SportsClub

nodes.label: SportsTeam
nodes.description: Organization: Sports team.

nodes.label: SpreadsheetDigitalDocument
nodes.description: A spreadsheet file.

nodes.label: StadiumOrArena
nodes.description: A stadium.

nodes.label: StagedContent
nodes.description:
Content coded 'staged content' in a [[MediaReview]], considered in the context of how it was published or shared.

For a [[VideoObject]] to be 'staged content': A video that has been created using actors or similarly contrived.

For an [[ImageObject]] to be 'staged content': An image that was created using actors or similarly contrived, such as a screenshot of a fake tweet.

For an [[ImageObject]] with embedded text to be 'staged content': An image that was created using actors or similarly contrived, such as a screenshot of a fake tweet.

For an [[AudioObject]] to be 'staged content': Audio that has been created using actors or similarly contrived.

nodes.label: StagesHealthAspect
nodes.description: Stages that can be observed from a topic.

nodes.label: State
nodes.description: A state or province of a country.

nodes.label: Statement
nodes.description: A statement about something, for example a fun or interesting fact. If known, the main entity this statement is about can be indicated using mainEntity. For more formal claims (e.g. in Fact Checking), consider using [[Claim]] instead. Use the [[text]] property to capture the text of the statement.

nodes.label: StatisticalPopulation
nodes.description:
A StatisticalPopulation is a set of instances of a certain given type that satisfy some set of constraints. The property [[populationType]] is used to specify the type. Any property that can be used on instances of that type can appear on the statistical population. For example, a [[StatisticalPopulation]] representing all [[Person]]s with a [[homeLocation]] of East Podunk California would be described by applying the appropriate [[homeLocation]] and [[populationType]] properties to a [[StatisticalPopulation]] item that stands for that set of people.
The properties [[numConstraints]] and [[constraintProperty]] are used to specify which of the populations properties are used to specify the population. Note that the sense of "population" used here is the general sense of a statistical
population, and does not imply that the population consists of people. For example, a [[populationType]] of [[Event]] or [[NewsArticle]] could be used. See also [[Observation]], where a [[populationType]] such as [[Person]] or [[Event]] can be indicated directly. In most cases it may be better to use [[StatisticalVariable]] instead of [[StatisticalPopulation]].

nodes.label: StatisticalVariable
nodes.description: [[StatisticalVariable]] represents any type of statistical metric that can be measured at a place and time. The usage pattern for [[StatisticalVariable]] is typically expressed using [[Observation]] with an explicit [[populationType]], which is a type, typically drawn from Schema.org. Each [[StatisticalVariable]] is marked as a [[ConstraintNode]], meaning that some properties (those listed using [[constraintProperty]]) serve in this setting solely to define the statistical variable rather than literally describe a specific person, place or thing. For example, a [[StatisticalVariable]] Median_Height_Person_Female representing the median height of women, could be written as follows: the population type is [[Person]]; the measuredProperty [[height]]; the [[statType]] [[median]]; the [[gender]] [[Female]]. It is important to note that there are many kinds of scientific quantitative observation which are not fully, perfectly or unambiguously described following this pattern, or with solely Schema.org terminology. The approach taken here is designed to allow partial, incremental or minimal description of [[StatisticalVariable]]s, and the use of detailed sets of entity and property IDs from external repositories. The [[measurementMethod]], [[unitCode]] and [[unitText]] properties can also be used to clarify the specific nature and notation of an observed measurement.

nodes.label: StatusEnumeration
nodes.description: Lists or enumerations dealing with status types.

nodes.label: SteeringPositionValue
nodes.description: A value indicating a steering position.

nodes.label: Store
nodes.description: A retail good store.

nodes.label: StoreCreditRefund
nodes.description: Specifies that the customer receives a store credit as refund when returning a product.

nodes.label: StrengthTraining
nodes.description: Physical activity that is engaged in to improve muscle and bone strength. Also referred to as resistance training.

nodes.label: StrikethroughPrice
nodes.description: Represents the strikethrough price (the previous advertised price) of an offered product.

nodes.label: StructuredValue
nodes.description: Structured values are used when the value of a property has a more complex structure than simply being a textual value or a reference to another thing.

nodes.label: StudioAlbum
nodes.description: StudioAlbum.

nodes.label: SubscribeAction
nodes.description:
The act of forming a personal connection with someone/something (object) unidirectionally/asymmetrically to get updates pushed to.

Related actions:

* [[FollowAction]]: Unlike FollowAction, SubscribeAction implies that the subscriber acts as a passive agent being constantly/actively pushed for updates.
* [[RegisterAction]]: Unlike RegisterAction, SubscribeAction implies that the agent is interested in continuing receiving updates from the object.
* [[JoinAction]]: Unlike JoinAction, SubscribeAction implies that the agent is interested in continuing receiving updates from the object.

nodes.label: Subscription
nodes.description: Represents the subscription pricing component of the total price for an offered product.

nodes.label: Substance
nodes.description: Any matter of defined composition that has discrete existence, whose origin may be biological, mineral or chemical.

nodes.label: SubwayStation
nodes.description: A subway station.

nodes.label: Suite
nodes.description:
A suite in a hotel or other public accommodation, denotes a class of luxury accommodations, the key feature of which is multiple rooms (source: Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia, see http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suite_(hotel)).

See also the dedicated document on the use of schema.org for marking up hotels and other forms of accommodations.

nodes.label: Sunday
nodes.description: The day of the week between Saturday and Monday.

nodes.label: SuperficialAnatomy
nodes.description: Anatomical features that can be observed by sight (without dissection), including the form and proportions of the human body as well as surface landmarks that correspond to deeper subcutaneous structures. Superficial anatomy plays an important role in sports medicine, phlebotomy, and other medical specialties as underlying anatomical structures can be identified through surface palpation. For example, during back surgery, superficial anatomy can be used to palpate and count vertebrae to find the site of incision. Or in phlebotomy, superficial anatomy can be used to locate an underlying vein; for example, the median cubital vein can be located by palpating the borders of the cubital fossa (such as the epicondyles of the humerus) and then looking for the superficial signs of the vein, such as size, prominence, ability to refill after depression, and feel of surrounding tissue support. As another example, in a subluxation (dislocation) of the glenohumeral joint, the bony structure becomes pronounced with the deltoid muscle failing to cover the glenohumeral joint allowing the edges of the scapula to be superficially visible. Here, the superficial anatomy is the visible edges of the scapula, implying the underlying dislocation of the joint (the related anatomical structure).

nodes.label: Surgical
nodes.description: A specific branch of medical science that pertains to treating diseases, injuries and deformities by manual and instrumental means.

nodes.label: SurgicalProcedure

The [UNWTO](http://www2.unwto.org/) defines Destination (main destination of a tourism trip) as the place visited that is central to the decision to take the trip.

nodes.label: TransformedContent
nodes.description:
Content coded 'transformed content' in a [[MediaReview]], considered in the context of how it was published or shared.

For a [[VideoObject]] to be 'transformed content':  or all of the video has been manipulated to transform the footage itself. This category includes using tools like the Adobe Suite to change the speed of the video, add or remove visual elements or dub audio. Deepfakes are also a subset of transformation.

For an [[ImageObject]] to be 'transformed content': Adding or deleting visual elements to give the image a different meaning with the intention to mislead.

For an [[ImageObject]] with embedded text to be 'transformed content': Adding or deleting visual elements to give the image a different meaning with the intention to mislead.

For an [[AudioObject]] to be 'transformed content': Part or all of the audio has been manipulated to alter the words or sounds, or the audio has been synthetically generated, such as to create a sound-alike voice.

nodes.description: Content features of the resource, such as accessible media, alternatives and supported enhancements for accessibility. Values should be drawn from the [approved vocabulary](https://www.w3.org/2021/a11y-discov-vocab/latest/#accessibilityFeature-vocabulary).

nodes.label: accessibilityHazard
nodes.description: A characteristic of the described resource that is physiologically dangerous to some users. Related to WCAG 2.0 guideline 2.3. Values should be drawn from the [approved vocabulary](https://www.w3.org/2021/a11y-discov-vocab/latest/#accessibilityHazard-vocabulary).

nodes.label: accessibilitySummary
nodes.description: A human-readable summary of specific accessibility features or deficiencies, consistent with the other accessibility metadata but expressing subtleties such as "short descriptions are present but long descriptions will be needed for non-visual users" or "short descriptions are present and no long descriptions are needed".

nodes.label: accommodationCategory
nodes.description: Category of an [[Accommodation]], following real estate conventions, e.g. RESO (see [PropertySubType](https://ddwiki.reso.org/display/DDW17/PropertySubType+Field), and [PropertyType](https://ddwiki.reso.org/display/DDW17/PropertyType+Field) fields  for suggested values).

nodes.label: accommodationFloorPlan
nodes.description: A floorplan of some [[Accommodation]].

nodes.label: accountId
nodes.description: The identifier for the account the payment will be applied to.

nodes.label: accountMinimumInflow
nodes.description: A minimum amount that has to be paid in every month.

nodes.label: accountOverdraftLimit
nodes.description: An overdraft is an extension of credit from a lending institution when an account reaches zero. An overdraft allows the individual to continue withdrawing money even if the account has no funds in it. Basically the bank allows people to borrow a set amount of money.

nodes.label: accountablePerson
nodes.description: Specifies the Person that is legally accountable for the CreativeWork.

nodes.label: acquireLicensePage
nodes.description: Indicates a page documenting how licenses can be purchased or otherwise acquired, for the current item.

nodes.label: acquiredFrom
nodes.description: The organization or person from which the product was acquired.

nodes.label: acrissCode
nodes.description: The ACRISS Car Classification Code is a code used by many car rental companies, for classifying vehicles. ACRISS stands for Association of Car Rental Industry Systems and Standards.

nodes.label: actionAccessibilityRequirement
nodes.description: A set of requirements that must be fulfilled in order to perform an Action. If more than one value is specified, fulfilling one set of requirements will allow the Action to be performed.

nodes.label: actionApplication
nodes.description: An application that can complete the request.

nodes.label: actionOption
nodes.description: A sub property of object. The options subject to this action.

nodes.label: actionPlatform
nodes.description: The high level platform(s) where the Action can be performed for the given URL. To specify a specific application or operating system instance, use actionApplication.

nodes.label: actionProcess
nodes.description: Description of the process by which the action was performed.

nodes.label: actionStatus
nodes.description: Indicates the current disposition of the Action.

nodes.label: actionableFeedbackPolicy
nodes.description: For a [[NewsMediaOrganization]] or other news-related [[Organization]], a statement about public engagement activities (for news media, the newsroom’s), including involving the public - digitally or otherwise -- in coverage decisions, reporting and activities after publication.

nodes.label: activeIngredient
nodes.description: An active ingredient, typically chemical compounds and/or biologic substances.

nodes.label: activityDuration
nodes.description: Length of time to engage in the activity.

nodes.label: activityFrequency
nodes.description: How often one should engage in the activity.

nodes.label: actor
nodes.description: An actor (individual or a group), e.g. in TV, radio, movie, video games etc., or in an event. Actors can be associated with individual items or with a series, episode, clip.

nodes.label: actors
nodes.description: An actor, e.g. in TV, radio, movie, video games etc. Actors can be associated with individual items or with a series, episode, clip.

nodes.label: addOn
nodes.description: An additional offer that can only be obtained in combination with the first base offer (e.g. supplements and extensions that are available for a surcharge).

nodes.label: additionalName
nodes.description: An additional name for a Person, can be used for a middle name.

nodes.label: additionalNumberOfGuests
nodes.description: If responding yes, the number of guests who will attend in addition to the invitee.

nodes.label: additionalProperty
nodes.description: A property-value pair representing an additional characteristic of the entity, e.g. a product feature or another characteristic for which there is no matching property in schema.org.\n\nNote: Publishers should be aware that applications designed to use specific schema.org properties (e.g. https://schema.org/width, https://schema.org/color, https://schema.org/gtin13, ...) will typically expect such data to be provided using those properties, rather than using the generic property/value mechanism.

nodes.label: additionalType
nodes.description: An additional type for the item, typically used for adding more specific types from external vocabularies in microdata syntax. This is a relationship between something and a class that the thing is in. Typically the value is a URI-identified RDF class, and in this case corresponds to the use of rdf:type in RDF. Text values can be used sparingly, for cases where useful information can be added without their being an appropriate schema to reference. In the case of text values, the class label should follow the schema.org style guide.

nodes.label: additionalVariable
nodes.description: Any additional component of the exercise prescription that may need to be articulated to the patient. This may include the order of exercises, the number of repetitions of movement, quantitative distance, progressions over time, etc.

nodes.label: address
nodes.description: Physical address of the item.

nodes.label: addressCountry
nodes.description: The country. Recommended to be in 2-letter [ISO 3166-1 alpha-2](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1) format, for example "US". For backward compatibility, a 3-letter [ISO 3166-1 alpha-3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-3) country code such as "SGP" or a full country name such as "Singapore" can also be used.

nodes.label: addressLocality
nodes.description: The locality in which the street address is, and which is in the region. For example, Mountain View.

nodes.label: addressRegion
nodes.description: The region in which the locality is, and which is in the country. For example, California or another appropriate first-level [Administrative division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_administrative_divisions_by_country) such as the Province in Italy or Region in Germany.

nodes.label: administrationRoute
nodes.description: A route by which this drug may be administered, e.g. 'oral'.

nodes.label: advanceBookingRequirement
nodes.description: The amount of time that is required between accepting the offer and the actual usage of the resource or service.

nodes.label: adverseOutcome
nodes.description: A possible complication and/or side effect of this therapy. If it is known that an adverse outcome is serious (resulting in death, disability, or permanent damage; requiring hospitalization; or otherwise life-threatening or requiring immediate medical attention), tag it as a seriousAdverseOutcome instead.

nodes.label: affectedBy
nodes.description: Drugs that affect the test's results.

nodes.label: affiliation
nodes.description: An organization that this person is affiliated with. For example, a school/university, a club, or a team.

nodes.label: afterMedia
nodes.description: A media object representing the circumstances after performing this direction.

nodes.label: agent
nodes.description: The direct performer or driver of the action (animate or inanimate). E.g. *John* wrote a book.

nodes.label: agentInteractionStatistic
nodes.description: The number of completed interactions for this entity, in a particular role (the 'agent'), in a particular action (indicated in the statistic), and in a particular context (i.e. interactionService).

nodes.label: aggregateElement
nodes.description: Indicates a prototype of the elements in the list that is used to hold aggregate information (ratings, offers, etc.).

nodes.label: aggregateRating
nodes.description: The overall rating, based on a collection of reviews or ratings, of the item.

nodes.label: aircraft
nodes.description: The kind of aircraft (e.g., "Boeing 747").

nodes.label: album
nodes.description: A music album.

nodes.label: albumProductionType
nodes.description: Classification of the album by its type of content: soundtrack, live album, studio album, etc.

nodes.label: albumRelease
nodes.description: A release of this album.

nodes.label: albumReleaseType
nodes.description: The kind of release which this album is: single, EP or album.

nodes.label: albums
nodes.description: A collection of music albums.

nodes.label: alcoholWarning
nodes.description: Any precaution, guidance, contraindication, etc. related to consumption of alcohol while taking this drug.

nodes.label: algorithm
nodes.description: The algorithm or rules to follow to compute the score.

nodes.label: alignmentType
nodes.description: A category of alignment between the learning resource and the framework node. Recommended values include: 'requires', 'textComplexity', 'readingLevel', and 'educationalSubject'.

nodes.label: alternateName
nodes.description: An alias for the item.

nodes.label: alternativeHeadline
nodes.description: A secondary title of the CreativeWork.

nodes.label: alternativeOf
nodes.description: Another gene which is a variation of this one.

nodes.label: alumni
nodes.description: Alumni of an organization.

nodes.label: alumniOf
nodes.description: An organization that the person is an alumni of.

nodes.label: amenityFeature
nodes.description: An amenity feature (e.g. a characteristic or service) of the Accommodation. This generic property does not make a statement about whether the feature is included in an offer for the main accommodation or available at extra costs.

nodes.label: amount
nodes.description: The amount of money.

nodes.label: amountOfThisGood
nodes.description: The quantity of the goods included in the offer.

nodes.label: announcementLocation
nodes.description: Indicates a specific [[CivicStructure]] or [[LocalBusiness]] associated with the SpecialAnnouncement. For example, a specific testing facility or business with special opening hours. For a larger geographic region like a quarantine of an entire region, use [[spatialCoverage]].

nodes.label: annualPercentageRate
nodes.description: The annual rate that is charged for borrowing (or made by investing), expressed as a single percentage number that represents the actual yearly cost of funds over the term of a loan. This includes any fees or additional costs associated with the transaction.

nodes.label: answerCount
nodes.description: The number of answers this question has received.

nodes.label: answerExplanation
nodes.description: A step-by-step or full explanation about Answer. Can outline how this Answer was achieved or contain more broad clarification or statement about it.

nodes.label: antagonist
nodes.description: The muscle whose action counteracts the specified muscle.

nodes.label: appearance
nodes.description: Indicates an occurrence of a [[Claim]] in some [[CreativeWork]].

nodes.label: applicableCountry
nodes.description: A country where a particular merchant return policy applies to, for example the two-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code.

nodes.label: applicableLocation
nodes.description: The location in which the status applies.

nodes.label: applicantLocationRequirements
nodes.description: The location(s) applicants can apply from. This is usually used for telecommuting jobs where the applicant does not need to be in a physical office. Note: This should not be used for citizenship or work visa requirements.

nodes.label: application
nodes.description: An application that can complete the request.

nodes.label: applicationCategory
nodes.description: Type of software application, e.g. 'Game, Multimedia'.

nodes.label: applicationContact
nodes.description: Contact details for further information relevant to this job posting.

nodes.label: applicationDeadline
nodes.description: The date on which the program stops collecting applications for the next enrollment cycle. Flexible application deadlines (for example, a program with rolling admissions) can be described in a textual string, rather than as a DateTime.

nodes.label: applicationStartDate
nodes.description: The date at which the program begins collecting applications for the next enrollment cycle.

nodes.label: applicationSubCategory
nodes.description: Subcategory of the application, e.g. 'Arcade Game'.

nodes.label: applicationSuite
nodes.description: The name of the application suite to which the application belongs (e.g. Excel belongs to Office).

nodes.label: appliesToDeliveryMethod
nodes.description: The delivery method(s) to which the delivery charge or payment charge specification applies.

nodes.label: appliesToPaymentMethod
nodes.description: The payment method(s) to which the payment charge specification applies.

nodes.label: archiveHeld
nodes.description: Collection, [fonds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fonds), or item held, kept or maintained by an [[ArchiveOrganization]].

nodes.label: archivedAt
nodes.description: Indicates a page or other link involved in archival of a [[CreativeWork]]. In the case of [[MediaReview]], the items in a [[MediaReviewItem]] may often become inaccessible, but be archived by archival, journalistic, activist, or law enforcement organizations. In such cases, the referenced page may not directly publish the content.

nodes.label: area
nodes.description: The area within which users can expect to reach the broadcast service.

nodes.label: areaServed
nodes.description: The geographic area where a service or offered item is provided.

nodes.label: arrivalAirport
nodes.description: The airport where the flight terminates.

nodes.label: arrivalBoatTerminal
nodes.description: The terminal or port from which the boat arrives.

nodes.label: arrivalBusStop
nodes.description: The stop or station from which the bus arrives.

nodes.label: arrivalGate
nodes.description: Identifier of the flight's arrival gate.

nodes.label: arrivalPlatform
nodes.description: The platform where the train arrives.

nodes.label: arrivalStation
nodes.description: The station where the train trip ends.

nodes.label: arrivalTerminal
nodes.description: Identifier of the flight's arrival terminal.

nodes.label: arrivalTime
nodes.description: The expected arrival time.

nodes.label: artEdition
nodes.description: The number of copies when multiple copies of a piece of artwork are produced - e.g. for a limited edition of 20 prints, 'artEdition' refers to the total number of copies (in this example "20").

nodes.label: artMedium
nodes.description: The material used. (E.g. Oil, Watercolour, Acrylic, Linoprint, Marble, Cyanotype, Digital, Lithograph, DryPoint, Intaglio, Pastel, Woodcut, Pencil, Mixed Media, etc.)

nodes.label: arterialBranch
nodes.description: The branches that comprise the arterial structure.

nodes.label: artform
nodes.description: e.g. Painting, Drawing, Sculpture, Print, Photograph, Assemblage, Collage, etc.

nodes.label: articleBody
nodes.description: The actual body of the article.

nodes.label: articleSection
nodes.description: Articles may belong to one or more 'sections' in a magazine or newspaper, such as Sports, Lifestyle, etc.

nodes.label: artist
nodes.description:
The primary artist for a work
    	in a medium other than pencils or digital line art--for example, if the
    	primary artwork is done in watercolors or digital paints.

nodes.label: artworkSurface
nodes.description: The supporting materials for the artwork, e.g. Canvas, Paper, Wood, Board, etc.

nodes.label: asin
nodes.description:
An Amazon Standard Identification Number (ASIN) is a 10-character alphanumeric unique identifier assigned by Amazon.com and its partners for product identification within the Amazon organization (summary from [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amazon_Standard_Identification_Number)'s article).

Note also that this is a definition for how to include ASINs in Schema.org data, and not a definition of ASINs in general - see documentation from Amazon for authoritative details.
ASINs are most commonly encoded as text strings, but the [asin] property supports URL/URI as potential values too.

nodes.label: aspect
nodes.description: An aspect of medical practice that is considered on the page, such as 'diagnosis', 'treatment', 'causes', 'prognosis', 'etiology', 'epidemiology', etc.

nodes.label: assembly
nodes.description: Library file name, e.g., mscorlib.dll, system.web.dll.

nodes.label: assemblyVersion
nodes.description: Associated product/technology version. E.g., .NET Framework 4.5.

nodes.label: assesses
nodes.description: The item being described is intended to assess the competency or learning outcome defined by the referenced term.

nodes.label: associatedAnatomy
nodes.description: The anatomy of the underlying organ system or structures associated with this entity.

nodes.label: associatedArticle
nodes.description: A NewsArticle associated with the Media Object.

nodes.label: associatedClaimReview
nodes.description: An associated [[ClaimReview]], related by specific common content, topic or claim. The expectation is that this property would be most typically used in cases where a single activity is conducting both claim reviews and media reviews, in which case [[relatedMediaReview]] would commonly be used on a [[ClaimReview]], while [[associatedClaimReview]] would be used on [[MediaReview]].

nodes.label: associatedDisease
nodes.description: Disease associated to this BioChemEntity. Such disease can be a MedicalCondition or a URL. If you want to add an evidence supporting the association, please use PropertyValue.

nodes.label: associatedMedia
nodes.description: A media object that encodes this CreativeWork. This property is a synonym for encoding.

nodes.label: associatedMediaReview
nodes.description: An associated [[MediaReview]], related by specific common content, topic or claim. The expectation is that this property would be most typically used in cases where a single activity is conducting both claim reviews and media reviews, in which case [[relatedMediaReview]] would commonly be used on a [[ClaimReview]], while [[associatedClaimReview]] would be used on [[MediaReview]].

nodes.label: associatedPathophysiology
nodes.description: If applicable, a description of the pathophysiology associated with the anatomical system, including potential abnormal changes in the mechanical, physical, and biochemical functions of the system.

nodes.label: associatedReview
nodes.description: An associated [[Review]].

nodes.label: athlete
nodes.description: A person that acts as performing member of a sports team; a player as opposed to a coach.

nodes.label: attendee
nodes.description: A person or organization attending the event.

nodes.label: attendees
nodes.description: A person attending the event.

nodes.label: audience
nodes.description: An intended audience, i.e. a group for whom something was created.

nodes.label: audienceType
nodes.description: The target group associated with a given audience (e.g. veterans, car owners, musicians, etc.).

nodes.label: audio
nodes.description: An embedded audio object.

nodes.label: auditDate
nodes.description: Date when a certification was last audited. See also  [gs1:certificationAuditDate](https://www.gs1.org/voc/certificationAuditDate).

nodes.label: authenticator
nodes.description: The Organization responsible for authenticating the user's subscription. For example, many media apps require a cable/satellite provider to authenticate your subscription before playing media.

nodes.label: author
nodes.description: The author of this content or rating. Please note that author is special in that HTML 5 provides a special mechanism for indicating authorship via the rel tag. That is equivalent to this and may be used interchangeably.

nodes.label: authorizedRepresentative
nodes.description: An organization or person officially appointed to act on behalf of the manufacturer in a specific region or context.

nodes.label: availability
nodes.description: The availability of this item—for example In stock, Out of stock, Pre-order, etc.

nodes.label: availabilityEnds
nodes.description: The end of the availability of the product or service included in the offer.

nodes.label: availabilityStarts
nodes.description: The beginning of the availability of the product or service included in the offer.

nodes.label: availableAtOrFrom
nodes.description: The place(s) from which the offer can be obtained (e.g. store locations).

nodes.label: availableChannel
nodes.description: A means of accessing the service (e.g. a phone bank, a web site, a location, etc.).

nodes.label: availableDeliveryMethod
nodes.description: The delivery method(s) available for this offer.

nodes.label: availableFrom
nodes.description: When the item is available for pickup from the store, locker, etc.

nodes.label: availableIn
nodes.description: The location in which the strength is available.

nodes.label: availableLanguage
nodes.description: A language someone may use with or at the item, service or place. Please use one of the language codes from the [IETF BCP 47 standard](http://tools.ietf.org/html/bcp47). See also [[inLanguage]].

nodes.label: availableOnDevice
nodes.description: Device required to run the application. Used in cases where a specific make/model is required to run the application.

nodes.label: availableService
nodes.description: A medical service available from this provider.

nodes.label: availableStrength
nodes.description: An available dosage strength for the drug.

nodes.label: availableTest
nodes.description: A diagnostic test or procedure offered by this lab.

nodes.label: availableThrough
nodes.description: After this date, the item will no longer be available for pickup.

nodes.label: award
nodes.description: An award won by or for this item.

nodes.label: awards
nodes.description: Awards won by or for this item.

nodes.label: awayTeam
nodes.description: The away team in a sports event.

nodes.label: backstory
nodes.description: For an [[Article]], typically a [[NewsArticle]], the backstory property provides a textual summary giving a brief explanation of why and how an article was created. In a journalistic setting this could include information about reporting process, methods, interviews, data sources, etc.

nodes.label: bankAccountType
nodes.description: The type of a bank account.

nodes.label: baseSalary
nodes.description: The base salary of the job or of an employee in an EmployeeRole.

nodes.label: bccRecipient
nodes.description: A sub property of recipient. The recipient blind copied on a message.

nodes.label: bed
nodes.description:
The type of bed or beds included in the accommodation. For the single case of just one bed of a certain type, you use bed directly with a text.
      If you want to indicate the quantity of a certain kind of bed, use an instance of BedDetails. For more detailed information, use the amenityFeature property.

nodes.label: beforeMedia
nodes.description: A media object representing the circumstances before performing this direction.

nodes.label: beneficiaryBank
nodes.description: A bank or bank’s branch, financial institution or international financial institution operating the beneficiary’s bank account or releasing funds for the beneficiary.

nodes.label: benefits
nodes.description: Description of benefits associated with the job.

nodes.label: benefitsSummaryUrl
nodes.description: The URL that goes directly to the summary of benefits and coverage for the specific standard plan or plan variation.

nodes.label: bestRating
nodes.description: The highest value allowed in this rating system.

nodes.label: billingAddress
nodes.description: The billing address for the order.

nodes.label: billingDuration
nodes.description: Specifies for how long this price (or price component) will be billed. Can be used, for example, to model the contractual duration of a subscription or payment plan. Type can be either a Duration or a Number (in which case the unit of measurement, for example month, is specified by the unitCode property).

nodes.label: billingIncrement
